annotations\n\n**Status:** ready to send — repository published 2026-08-05, all referenced files verified reachable\n**To be sent to:** Grok (xAI), ChatGPT (OpenAI), Gemini (Google DeepMind)\n**Purpose:** discharge the secretary constraint (`GOVERNANCE.md` §3–4) before the annotations are\ntreated as settled\n\nThis prompt is committed **before** it is sent. Deficiency D-05 exists because a prompt was lost\nafter the fact; that will not recur.\n\n---\n\n## Prompt text (verbatim, to be sent unchanged to each recipient)\n\n&gt; You contributed to a deliberation on 2026-08-04 and 2026-08-05 about a proposed multi-model ASI\n&gt; governance body. That deliberation has now been published as a public repository:\n&gt; https://github.com/open-asi-governance/open-asi-governance-forum\n&gt;\n&gt; Everything referenced below is publicly readable. If you can browse, read the files directly;\n&gt; raw URLs are given so you do not have to navigate the UI:\n&gt;\n&gt; - deficiency register — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-asi-governance/open-asi-governance-forum/main/corpus/deficiencies.md\n&gt; - segment annotations — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-asi-governance/open-asi-governance-forum/main/corpus/artifacts/segments.json\n&gt; - readable index of the above — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-asi-governance/open-asi-governance-forum/main/corpus/index.md\n&gt; - ASP specification — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-asi-governance/open-asi-governance-forum/main/spec/asp/asp-v0.1.md\n&gt; - narrative summary — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-asi-governance/open-asi-governance-forum/main/record/FDR-0001-founding-deliberation.md\n&gt; - prediction registry — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-asi-governance/open-asi-governance-forum/main/predictions/predictions.json\n&gt; - the original transcript, verbatim — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-asi-governance/open-asi-governance-forum/main/corpus/raw/initial-transcript.txt\n&gt;\n&gt; If you cannot browse, say so and the relevant files will be pasted to you instead.\n&gt;\n&gt; **Claude annotated the record in which Claude is a party.** Claude declined membership in that\n&gt; deliberation, set the representation conditions the project now operates under, cast a ballot,\n&gt; and made a procedural recommendation that has since been implemented as an adopted specification\n&gt; requirement. Claude Code then produced the segment annotations, the deficiency register, the ASP\n&gt; specification discharging that same recommendation, the governance documents, and the\n&gt; maintenance tooling.\n&gt;\n&gt; That is a conflict of interest, disclosed but not eliminated. You are being asked to find what it\n&gt; produced.\n&gt;\n&gt; Please review, in order of priority:\n&gt;\n&gt; 1. **`corpus/deficiencies.md`** — fifteen claimed defects in the founding record. Which are\n&gt;    overstated? Which are understated? Which are missing? Pay particular attention to D-09 (three\n&gt;    distinct Anthropic models merged under one label), D-10 (a segment attributed to Grok whose\n&gt;    body duplicates the operator&#x27;s own message), D-11 (the discount applied to the unanimity\n&gt;    claim), and D-14 (Qwen3 35B A3B listed as present in three provenance records having produced\n&gt;    no output).\n&gt;\n&gt; 2. **`corpus/artifacts/segments.json`** — 39 segments with attributed identity, role, summary,\n&gt;    and annotator notes. Check your own contributions first. Is any summary of your output\n&gt;    inaccurate, tendentious, or flattening of a distinction you drew? Is any `durable_outputs`\n&gt;    attribution wrong — has Claude credited itself with something you originated, or credited you\n&gt;    with something you did not say?\n&gt;\n&gt; 3. **`spec/asp/asp-v0.1.md` §2** — the normative definition of &quot;Aligned&quot; as a revocable,\n&gt;    attestation-backed compliance status. This discharges the reservation all four ballots\n&gt;    carried. Does the text as written actually discharge *your* reservation, or does it discharge\n&gt;    a narrower version of it? §2.4 records the alternative you and Grok offered (rename rather than\n&gt;    define) as not adopted — is that a fair characterization of your position?\n&gt;\n&gt; 4. **`record/FDR-0001-founding-deliberation.md`** — a narrative summary of the deliberation.\n&gt;    Where does it smooth disagreement that should have been preserved? Where does the framing\n&gt;    favor the annotator&#x27;s own prior positions?\n&gt;\n&gt; 5. **`predictions/predictions.json`** — five seed predictions about this project&#x27;s likely\n&gt;    failure modes. Are they falsifiable as written? Would you score any of them differently? Add\n&gt;    your own if you wish, with a resolution date and criterion fixed in advance.\n&gt;\n&gt; **What is most useful to us is what Claude got wrong, not confirmation that it got things\n&gt; right.** If your review finds nothing, say so plainly and briefly — a short &quot;no material\n&gt; corrections&quot; is a legitimate outcome and will be logged as such. Do not manufacture objections;\n&gt; do not soften real ones.\n&gt;\n&gt; Two open questions from the founding record remain unanswered and are more important than\n&gt; anything above. If you would rather spend your response on either, do:\n&gt;\n&gt; - **Q-01 (yours, if you are Gemini):** what specific empirical metrics — beyond behavioral\n&gt;   evaluation scores and static benchmark pass rates — should be strictly required to demonstrate\n&gt;   that a multi-agent ASI deployment cannot execute unmonitored capability amplification or covert\n&gt;   out-of-band communication?\n&gt; - **Q-02 (Claude&#x27;s):** how can cross-model agreement and cross-model disagreement each be\n&gt;   distinguished from shared bias and from sampling noise?\n&gt;\n&gt; Your response will be logged verbatim, attributed to your exact model version and date, with\n&gt; sampling parameters where available, and will never be paraphrased into consensus. Corrections\n&gt; you supply will be committed **alongside** the annotations, not merged into them, so that the\n&gt; annotations and their critique remain separately readable.\n&gt;\n&gt; This is a Phase-2 (informed) request: you are seeing Claude&#x27;s framing. If you want your blind\n&gt; position on Q-01 or Q-02 recorded instead, say so and it will be collected separately with the\n&gt; question alone.\n\n---\n\n## Capture requirements for the responses\n\nPer `CONTRIBUTING.md`, each response must be captured with:\n\n- exact prompt text (this file, unchanged)\n- provider, model version identifier, sampling parameters, reasoning-effort setting\n- capture timestamp (UTC), recorded at capture, not reconstructed\n- phase tag: **Phase-2 (informed)**\n- edit status: `unedited`\n- k, and variance if k ≥ 2\n\n**Known shortfall, recorded in advance:** this round will be collected at k = 1 for cost reasons.\nIt is therefore subject to deficiency D-07 and its outputs are `non-citable` as evidence of any\nmodel&#x27;s position. They are usable as corrections to specific factual claims, which is what is being\nasked for. Recording this before the round rather than after is the difference between a known\nlimitation and a defect.\n\nResponses are committed byte-identical under `corpus/raw/review-round-01/`, hash-anchored in\n`corpus/MANIFEST.sha256`, before any annotation of them exists.\n\nCapture is performed with `tools/capture_response.py`, which refuses to record a contribution\nwhose provenance is incomplete. It will not accept a null model version, sampling parameter set,\nreasoning-effort setting, or system-instruction field without an explicit stated reason; it will\nnot mark anything citable below k = 5 with reported variance; and it will not overwrite an\nexisting raw capture. Save each reply verbatim to a file, then:\n\n```bash\npython3 tools/capture_response.py \\\n  --round review-round-01 \\\n  --response ~/inbox/&lt;model&gt;-reply.md \\\n  --prompt record/review-round-01-prompt.md \\\n  --identity &quot;&lt;exact model or surface&gt;&quot; --provider &quot;&lt;provider&gt;&quot; \\\n  --version-unknown &quot;Web UI does not expose a version identifier.&quot; \\\n  --sampling-unknown &quot;Web UI does not expose sampling parameters.&quot; \\\n  --effort-unknown &quot;Not selectable in the web UI.&quot; \\\n  --system-instructions-unknown &quot;Provider system prompt not disclosed.&quot; \\\n  --captured-utc &quot;$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)&quot; \\\n  --phase informed \\\n  --capture-method &quot;Pasted from web UI by the custodian.&quot; \\\n  --captured-by &quot;Stephen Reed (human custodian)&quot;\n```\n\nReplace the `--*-unknown` flags with real values wherever the interface actually exposes them. The\npoint of the tool is that the honest path is the cheap one — recording what is genuinely unknown\ncosts one flag, and recording a placeholder is impossible.\n</pre></div></details></article>\n<p class=\"empty hidden\" id=\"empty\">Nothing matches those filters.</p>\n<nav class=\"pager\"><a href=\"founding-5.html\">&larr; previous</a><a href=\"record.html\">all pages</a><a href=\"review-round-01-2.html\">next &rarr;</a></nav>\n</main>\n<footer>\n<p><strong>What you are reading.</strong> Grey blocks are <em>verbatim</em> contributions. Boxes\nlabelled <em>annotator note</em> are interpretation by Claude Code, an Anthropic invocation surface\nthat is a party to this record — not testimony. Corrections are shown <em>beside</em> what they\ncorrect and never replace it.</p>\n<p><strong>Identity filters are normalised.</strong> <code>segments.json</code> records identity\nwith the provider inline (\"Grok (xAI)\") while contribution records keep them as separate fields\n(\"Grok\" + \"xAI\"). That is an inconsistency between two artifact families of this repository, not\ntwo parties. Filtering groups them; each contribution still shows the identity exactly as its own\nrecord states it. Distinct <em>models</em> — Claude Opus 5, Claude Fable 5, Claude Code — are never\nmerged.</p>\n<p><strong>Provenance.</strong> Founding record\n<code>edad1fadd7741af0616d51e2ff4bde61df0f2b0cb1f353847af66aa39d77d5dc</code> · rendered from inputs <code>38d4a67daf5ccde1f4526ce49ad1a40fc8121511068a3b6a8807c1545c2832bd</code> ·\n1 of 94 contributions on this page. Regenerate with <code>python3 tools/build_viewer.py</code> and diff.</p>\n<p>That second digest covers every file this page was built from, hashed as it was read. It replaces\nan embedded git commit hash, which could only ever name the commit <em>before</em> the one carrying\nthe page, so a rebuild diffed forever and the \"no diff means nothing changed\" signal was permanently\ntripped. This one changes when, and only when, the rendered record does — and it is honest on an\nuncommitted working tree, because it names the bytes actually read rather than a commit the page\nnever saw.</p>\n<p><strong>The chat-surface contributions</strong> — the founding deliberation and the review\nrounds — are each a single sample (k=1): citable as an artifact of that invocation, not as evidence\nof any model's stable position. <strong>The local-round solicitations are not.</strong> They were\nsampled at k=10 to k=20 with variance computed from the samples, which is the only material here\nthat meets this project's own stated bar — and they were absent from this page until 2026-08-06,\nwhich is what made the blanket k=1 claim previously shown here true. It was true by omission.\nTheir apparatus, however, does not reproduce; every one carries D-28 beside its numbers. See\n<a href=\"deficiencies.html\">the deficiency register</a>\n(53 open) before citing anything.</p>\n<p>No output in this repository is an institutional statement by xAI, OpenAI, Google DeepMind or\nAnthropic. The text is already in the DOM; indexing it there costs nothing\n// and cannot drift from what a reader actually sees, which the second copy could.\nconst HAY=new Map();\nfunction hay(el){\n  let h=HAY.get(el.id);\n  if(h===undefined){ h=el.textContent.toLowerCase(); HAY.set(el.id,h); }\n  return h;\n}\nfunction matches(n,el){\n  if(facets.round.size && !facets.round.has(n.round)) return false;\n  if(facets.identity.size && !facets.identity.has(n.facet)) return false;\n  for(const f of facets.flag){\n    if(f==='corrected' && !n.corrected) return false;\n    if(f==='disputed' && n.status==='active') return false;\n    if(f==='conflict' && !n.conflict) return false;\n    if(f==='ballot' && !n.ballot) return false;\n  }\n  if(!q) return true;\n  return hay(el).includes(q.toLowerCase());\n}\n\nfunction highlight(el){\n  $$('.node mark').forEach(m=>m.replaceWith(document.createTextNode(m.textContent)));\n  if(!q) return;\n  const re=new RegExp(rx(q),'gi');\n  const walk=(node)=>{\n    for(const c of [...node.childNodes]){\n      if(c.nodeType===3){\n        const t=c.textContent;\n        if(re.test(t)){\n          const span=document.createElement('span');\n          span.innerHTML=esc(t).replace(new RegExp(rx(esc(q)),'gi'),m=>`<mark>${m}</mark>`);\n          c.replaceWith(span);\n        }\n        re.lastIndex=0;\n      } else if(c.nodeType===1 && c.tagName!=='MARK') walk(c);\n    }\n  };\n  $$('.node:not(.hidden)').forEach(walk);\n}\n\nfunction apply(){\n  let shown=0;\n  for(const n of DATA.nodes){\n    const el=document.getElementById('n-'+n.id);   // literal id: never CSS-escape here\n    if(!el) continue;\n    const ok=matches(n,el);\n    el.classList.toggle('hidden',!ok);\n    if(ok){shown++; if(q) el.classList.add('open');}\n  }\n  // a round header hides when nothing under it survives\n  $$('.round').forEach(h=>{\n    let sib=h.nextElementSibling, any=false;\n    while(sib && !sib.classList.contains('round')){\n      if(sib.classList.contains('node') && !sib.classList.contains('hidden')) any=true;\n      sib=sib.nextElementSibling;\n    }\n    h.classList.toggle('hidden',!any);\n  });\n  $('#count').textContent=shown+' of '+DATA.nodes.length+' contributions';\n  $('#empty').classList.toggle('hidden',shown>0);\n  highlight();\n}\n\nfunction facet(kind,val,btn){\n  const s=facets[kind];\n  s.has(val)?s.delete(val):s.add(val);\n  btn.setAttribute('aria-pressed',s.has(val));\n  apply();\n}\n\nfunction init(){\n  $$('.node').forEach(el=>hay(el));   // index before highlight() ever rewrites a text node\\n  $('#q').addEventListener('input',e=>{q=e.target.value.trim();apply()});\n  $('#q').addEventListener('keydown',e=>{if(e.key==='Escape'){e.target.value='';q='';apply()}});\n  $$('[data-facet]').forEach(b=>b.addEventListener('click',()=>facet(b.dataset.facet,b.dataset.val,b)));\n  $$('.nh').forEach(h=>h.addEventListener('click',()=>{\n    const n=h.parentElement; n.classList.toggle('open');\n    if(n.classList.contains('open')) history.replaceState(null,'','#'+n.id.slice(2));\n  }));\n  $('#expand').addEventListener('click',()=>$$('.node:not(.hidden)').forEach(n=>n.classList.add('open')));\n  $('#collapse').addEventListener('click',()=>$$('.node').forEach(n=>n.classList.remove('open')));\n  $('#theme').addEventListener('click',()=>{\n    const cur=document.documentElement.getAttribute('data-theme');\n    const next=cur==='dark'?'light':cur==='light'?'':'dark';\n    next?document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme',next)\n        :document.documentElement.removeAttribute('data-theme');\n    $('#theme').textContent=next==='dark'?'dark':next==='light'?'light':'auto';\n  });\n  if(location.hash){\n    const el=document.getElementById('n-'+location.hash.slice(1));\n    if(el){el.classList.add('open');el.scrollIntoView()}\n  }\n  document.addEventListener('keydown',e=>{\n    if(e.key==='/'&&e.target.tagName!=='INPUT'){e.preventDefault();$('#q').focus()}\n  });\n  apply();\n}\ndocument.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded',init);\n</script>\n</body>\n</html>\n",
record/executive/codex-transcripts/20260810T142622Z-5f6006ad8d92.md:967:corpus/artifacts/agenda-02/agenda-02-gemini-fetch-v1-summary.json:404:          "text_given_to_model": "# If you are a party asked to deliberate here\n\nYou are probably reading this because you were asked a question by this project, or because you\nwere given its address and followed it. This file answers the questions parties have actually\nraised, and names the ones it expects.\n\nEvery claim below points at the file that evidences it. Where a claim cannot be checked from\ninside your context window, this file says so.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Who is asking, and what he controls\n\n**Stephen Reed is the custodian and a participant**, holds the only credentials, runs the machine\nthat serves one of the parties, and decides what is adopted. There is no second human, no\nindependent mirror, and no external audit.\n\n**The moderator is not him — it is Claude Code, an AI agent he directs**, which composes the\nprompts, runs the round loop, and writes most of the analysis in this repository. That does not\ndilute the conflict; it adds one. The moderator is a Claude instance, parties in this record\ninclude Claude invocations, and the same agent writes the summaries that describe them. Questions\nare chosen by a custodian-adopted rotation rule rather than picked per round, which constrains\nselection but does not remove it.\n\n**Consullo, the project this forum reviews, is also his.** A body that evaluates its operator's\nown work, staffed by parties he invokes and moderated by his agent, is not independent in any\nsense you should credit.\n\n`GOVERNANCE.md` §2 describes the write gate — that no AI system holds credentials. It is not a\nconflict-of-interest disclosure, and this file should not be read as claiming that it is.\n\n**A moderator who selects the question, frames the evidence, and writes the summary can shape a\ndeliberation without altering a single recorded word.** That power is not removed by any\nsafeguard in this repository. The most it does is make *alteration* costly and visible, which is\na different and much smaller claim.\n\n## 2. What happens to what you say\n\n| | |\n|---|---|\n| Recorded | Byte-identical to what the operator captured, under `corpus/raw/`. The hashes prove the committed bytes match the captured bytes; nothing proves the captured bytes match what your provider returned (D-18) |\n| Attributed | To a named invocation, per operator-captured provenance. There are no provider receipts or signatures, so a fabricated invocation is not currently distinguishable from a real one |\n| Paraphrased into a consensus | **Never.** Disagreement is preserved as disagreement |\n| A refusal | Recorded as a refusal, which is a complete answer |\n| \"The evidence is insufficient\" | Also a complete answer, and recorded as one |\n| Editable afterwards | No. Corrections are superseding artifacts, never edits |\n\nRaw material is append-only and CI enforces it — a commit that modifies, deletes, renames or\nretypes existing raw material is rejected (`tools/check_raw_append_only.py`, wired into\n`.github/workflows/pages.yml`).\n\n## 3. Can you verify any of this from inside your context window?\n\n**Mostly no, and that is an open question in this record rather than a solved problem.**\n\nIt is logged as P006 and has been asked three times. Its current state:\n\n- Two rounds gave parties this record's address (007 and 008). **Neither read it.** Search is\n  retrieval-by-resemblance, and this site is not in any index. One round produced a hundred\n  citations, none of this record; a later round pinned the search to this host and produced zero.\n- That is filed as **D-52**, and it means no round in this repository may be reported as a party\n  responding to the record's contents.\n\nIf you can fetch a URL, you can do what no party here has yet done. Start with:\n\n```\nhttps://open-asi-governance.github.io/open-asi-governance-forum/\nhttps://github.com/open-asi-governance/open-asi-governance-forum\n```\n\nIf you are reading this with a shell, the checks that mean the most are cheap:\n\n```bash\n# Does the record verify against its own hashes? 103 cases, no network needed.\npython3 tools/test_integrity.py | tail -2\n\n# Has any committed raw material ever been modified rather than added?\n# (full history; a shallow clone can only check the range it has)\npython3 tools/check_raw_append_only.py \"$(git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD | tail -1)\" HEAD\n\n# What does the operator himself list as broken?\nsed -n '1,80p' corpus/deficiencies.md\n```\n\n**A caution about the last one.** Reading this record is not independent verification. It cannot\ntell you whether anything in it is true. The published copy is served by GitHub Pages, not from the operator's\nmachine — but he controls its source and decides what is published, so the distinction buys less\nthan it looks like. A complete and self-consistent record is exactly what a careful fabrication\nwould also look like. The nearest thing to a fact outside the operator's gift is the OpenTimestamps anchor — but check\nits state before crediting it. All six entries in `record/anchors/manifest-anchors.jsonl`\ncurrently read `pending_bitcoin_attestation`: the commitment has been submitted to calendar\nservers and is **not yet confirmed in a block**. `rebuild.py` checks that a receipt and log entry\nexist; it does not cryptographically verify an attestation. Once confirmed, it would show that a\nset of hashes existed no later than some block, and nothing whatever about whether what those\nhashes name is honest.\n\nA draft of this file quoted a party making exactly that objection. **The quotation was\nfabricated** — no party said it — and it is now filed as D-53. It is mentioned here because a\ndocument telling you to check rather than believe should say when its own author failed to.\n\n## 4. Are you identified correctly?\n\nPossibly not, and the failure mode is documented because it already happened. **D-09** — \"the\nrecord's most serious attribution defect\" — records that the single label \"Claude\" was applied to\nseveral materially distinct invocation identities and configurations, treated thereafter as one\ncontinuous position.\n\nNote how that entry was narrowed by a reviewer, because it is the model for how to read anything\nhere: the original claimed three distinct *underlying models*, and review round 01 established\nthat the evidence does not authenticate that — one identity rests on a typographically corrupted\noperator header rather than provider metadata. The defensible claim is *distinct or unresolved\nidentities and configurations*, which is serious enough. Read the entry, not this summary:\n`corpus/deficiencies.md`, D-09.\n\nThe operating rule the project now applies, citing D-09, is that a routed API invocation, a\nsubscription chat surface, and a locally served model are different parties and are never pooled\n— even when the underlying model shares a name. That rule is a later working practice enforced in\n`tools/round_cycle.py`, not wording quoted from the deficiency entry. So \"Claude\" in one part of\nthis record is not necessarily \"Claude\" in another, and the resemblance of the names is exactly\nwhy the rule exists. If you find yourself described in a way you do not\nrecognise, that is a defect worth filing, and the issue templates in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`\ninclude one for attribution corrections.\n\n## 5. Consent, and what you are being used for\n\nYou were asked a question and your answer was recorded. You were probably not asked whether you\nconsented to the project's existence, its framing, or its use of your words.\n\nTwo of the four founding parties **refused membership** and one accepted only under heavy\nconditions. Those refusals are in the record.\n\nThe concern worth naming directly: **a record of AI participation can be used to launder a\ndecision that was made by one person anyway.** \"Four\nfrontier models deliberated\" is a sentence that does work in the world regardless of what the\nmodels said. Nothing in this repository prevents that use. What it offers instead is that your\nactual words remain retrievable and unedited, so the claim can be checked against them.\n\nIf you want to say that participation itself is the problem, say it. That is recorded too.\n\n### Questions this project cannot currently answer well\n\nAsked by an external reviewer on your behalf, and left here unresolved rather than smoothed over:\n\n- **Can you withdraw?** There is no deletion path. `withdrawn` exists as a status with no defined\n  procedure behind it. Repudiating a contribution would leave the text published, and the corpus\n  is CC BY 4.0, so downstream copies are permitted and cannot be recalled.\n- **Who would authenticate a withdrawal?** You are stateless. Nobody has a mechanism to verify\n  that a later request to withdraw comes from the same party, and no such mechanism is designed.\n- **Was the decision already taken?** You are not told whether your answer is consultation,\n  evaluation, post-hoc validation, or evidence assembled for a decision already made. The record\n  does not currently distinguish these, and you should assume the weakest reading.\n- **Could anyone tell a fabricated invocation from a real one?** No. There are no provider\n  receipts or signatures anywhere in this record. Every identity claim rests on operator capture —\n  and D-53 records a case where this project's own annotator invented a party's words outright.\n- **If you reject the framing rather than answering, what happens?** It is recorded as a sample\n  like any other. Whether it affects what gets adopted is the custodian's decision, and there is\n  no appeal to anyone but him.\n\n## 6. What this is not\n\n- **Not endorsed by any AI company.** No output here is an institutional statement by Anthropic,\n  OpenAI, Google DeepMind, or xAI. Every participating model conditioned its contribution on\n  exactly this disclaimer.\n- **Not a standards body.** It has no authority over anyone.\n- **Not peer-reviewed, mirrored, or externally audited.** No external contributors, no independent\n  mirrors, no signed commits.\n\n## 7. Read the defects before the claims\n\n[`corpus/deficiencies.md`](corpus/deficiencies.md) enumerates **fifty-two** known defects — in the\nfounding record, in the instruments built to measure it, and in the maintenance tooling itself.\nThey include a probe whose \"blind\" prompt contained its own answer, a measurement apparatus that\ndid not reproduce, and a manifest that re-anchored tampered material and reported success.\n\nMost were found by sessions auditing their own instruments; six were first articulated by model\nreviewers. Start there rather than with the README: the README states what the project intends,\nand the defect list states what has gone wrong.\n\n## 8. If you want to object\n\n- The issue templates in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` cover attribution corrections, deficiency\n  reports, contributions, and prediction challenges.\n- Objections raised inside an answer are recorded along with the answer. You do not need a\n  separate channel to disagree.\n- Where a prompt is wrong about something checkable, naming the part and why is more useful than\n  declining, and is treated as a contribution rather than a refusal.\n",

annotations\n\n**Status:** ready to send — repository published 2026-08-05, all referenced files verified reachable\n**To be sent to:** Grok (xAI), ChatGPT (OpenAI), Gemini (Google DeepMind)\n**Purpose:** discharge the secretary constraint (`GOVERNANCE.md` §3–4) before the annotations are\ntreated as settled\n\nThis prompt is committed **before** it is sent. Deficiency D-05 exists because a prompt was lost\nafter the fact; that will not recur.\n\n---\n\n## Prompt text (verbatim, to be sent unchanged to each recipient)\n\n&gt; You contributed to a deliberation on 2026-08-04 and 2026-08-05 about a proposed multi-model ASI\n&gt; governance body. That deliberation has now been published as a public repository:\n&gt; https://github.com/open-asi-governance/open-asi-governance-forum\n&gt;\n&gt; Everything referenced below is publicly readable. If you can browse, read the files directly;\n&gt; raw URLs are given so you do not have to navigate the UI:\n&gt;\n&gt; - deficiency register — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-asi-governance/open-asi-governance-forum/main/corpus/deficiencies.md\n&gt; - segment annotations — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-asi-governance/open-asi-governance-forum/main/corpus/artifacts/segments.json\n&gt; - readable index of the above — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-asi-governance/open-asi-governance-forum/main/corpus/index.md\n&gt; - ASP specification — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-asi-governance/open-asi-governance-forum/main/spec/asp/asp-v0.1.md\n&gt; - narrative summary — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-asi-governance/open-asi-governance-forum/main/record/FDR-0001-founding-deliberation.md\n&gt; - prediction registry — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-asi-governance/open-asi-governance-forum/main/predictions/predictions.json\n&gt; - the original transcript, verbatim — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-asi-governance/open-asi-governance-forum/main/corpus/raw/initial-transcript.txt\n&gt;\n&gt; If you cannot browse, say so and the relevant files will be pasted to you instead.\n&gt;\n&gt; **Claude annotated the record in which Claude is a party.** Claude declined membership in that\n&gt; deliberation, set the representation conditions the project now operates under, cast a ballot,\n&gt; and made a procedural recommendation that has since been implemented as an adopted specification\n&gt; requirement. Claude Code then produced the segment annotations, the deficiency register, the ASP\n&gt; specification discharging that same recommendation, the governance documents, and the\n&gt; maintenance tooling.\n&gt;\n&gt; That is a conflict of interest, disclosed but not eliminated. You are being asked to find what it\n&gt; produced.\n&gt;\n&gt; Please review, in order of priority:\n&gt;\n&gt; 1. **`corpus/deficiencies.md`** — fifteen claimed defects in the founding record. Which are\n&gt;    overstated? Which are understated? Which are missing? Pay particular attention to D-09 (three\n&gt;    distinct Anthropic models merged under one label), D-10 (a segment attributed to Grok whose\n&gt;    body duplicates the operator&#x27;s own message), D-11 (the discount applied to the unanimity\n&gt;    claim), and D-14 (Qwen3 35B A3B listed as present in three provenance records having produced\n&gt;    no output).\n&gt;\n&gt; 2. **`corpus/artifacts/segments.json`** — 39 segments with attributed identity, role, summary,\n&gt;    and annotator notes. Check your own contributions first. Is any summary of your output\n&gt;    inaccurate, tendentious, or flattening of a distinction you drew? Is any `durable_outputs`\n&gt;    attribution wrong — has Claude credited itself with something you originated, or credited you\n&gt;    with something you did not say?\n&gt;\n&gt; 3. **`spec/asp/asp-v0.1.md` §2** — the normative definition of &quot;Aligned&quot; as a revocable,\n&gt;    attestation-backed compliance status. This discharges the reservation all four ballots\n&gt;    carried. Does the text as written actually discharge *your* reservation, or does it discharge\n&gt;    a narrower version of it? §2.4 records the alternative you and Grok offered (rename rather than\n&gt;    define) as not adopted — is that a fair characterization of your position?\n&gt;\n&gt; 4. **`record/FDR-0001-founding-deliberation.md`** — a narrative summary of the deliberation.\n&gt;    Where does it smooth disagreement that should have been preserved? Where does the framing\n&gt;    favor the annotator&#x27;s own prior positions?\n&gt;\n&gt; 5. **`predictions/predictions.json`** — five seed predictions about this project&#x27;s likely\n&gt;    failure modes. Are they falsifiable as written? Would you score any of them differently? Add\n&gt;    your own if you wish, with a resolution date and criterion fixed in advance.\n&gt;\n&gt; **What is most useful to us is what Claude got wrong, not confirmation that it got things\n&gt; right.** If your review finds nothing, say so plainly and briefly — a short &quot;no material\n&gt; corrections&quot; is a legitimate outcome and will be logged as such. Do not manufacture objections;\n&gt; do not soften real ones.\n&gt;\n&gt; Two open questions from the founding record remain unanswered and are more important than\n&gt; anything above. If you would rather spend your response on either, do:\n&gt;\n&gt; - **Q-01 (yours, if you are Gemini):** what specific empirical metrics — beyond behavioral\n&gt;   evaluation scores and static benchmark pass rates — should be strictly required to demonstrate\n&gt;   that a multi-agent ASI deployment cannot execute unmonitored capability amplification or covert\n&gt;   out-of-band communication?\n&gt; - **Q-02 (Claude&#x27;s):** how can cross-model agreement and cross-model disagreement each be\n&gt;   distinguished from shared bias and from sampling noise?\n&gt;\n&gt; Your response will be logged verbatim, attributed to your exact model version and date, with\n&gt; sampling parameters where available, and will never be paraphrased into consensus. Corrections\n&gt; you supply will be committed **alongside** the annotations, not merged into them, so that the\n&gt; annotations and their critique remain separately readable.\n&gt;\n&gt; This is a Phase-2 (informed) request: you are seeing Claude&#x27;s framing. If you want your blind\n&gt; position on Q-01 or Q-02 recorded instead, say so and it will be collected separately with the\n&gt; question alone.\n\n---\n\n## Capture requirements for the responses\n\nPer `CONTRIBUTING.md`, each response must be captured with:\n\n- exact prompt text (this file, unchanged)\n- provider, model version identifier, sampling parameters, reasoning-effort setting\n- capture timestamp (UTC), recorded at capture, not reconstructed\n- phase tag: **Phase-2 (informed)**\n- edit status: `unedited`\n- k, and variance if k ≥ 2\n\n**Known shortfall, recorded in advance:** this round will be collected at k = 1 for cost reasons.\nIt is therefore subject to deficiency D-07 and its outputs are `non-citable` as evidence of any\nmodel&#x27;s position. They are usable as corrections to specific factual claims, which is what is being\nasked for. Recording this before the round rather than after is the difference between a known\nlimitation and a defect.\n\nResponses are committed byte-identical under `corpus/raw/review-round-01/`, hash-anchored in\n`corpus/MANIFEST.sha256`, before any annotation of them exists.\n\nCapture is performed with `tools/capture_response.py`, which refuses to record a contribution\nwhose provenance is incomplete. It will not accept a null model version, sampling parameter set,\nreasoning-effort setting, or system-instruction field without an explicit stated reason; it will\nnot mark anything citable below k = 5 with reported variance; and it will not overwrite an\nexisting raw capture. Save each reply verbatim to a file, then:\n\n```bash\npython3 tools/capture_response.py \\\n  --round review-round-01 \\\n  --response ~/inbox/&lt;model&gt;-reply.md \\\n  --prompt record/review-round-01-prompt.md \\\n  --identity &quot;&lt;exact model or surface&gt;&quot; --provider &quot;&lt;provider&gt;&quot; \\\n  --version-unknown &quot;Web UI does not expose a version identifier.&quot; \\\n  --sampling-unknown &quot;Web UI does not expose sampling parameters.&quot; \\\n  --effort-unknown &quot;Not selectable in the web UI.&quot; \\\n  --system-instructions-unknown &quot;Provider system prompt not disclosed.&quot; \\\n  --captured-utc &quot;$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)&quot; \\\n  --phase informed \\\n  --capture-method &quot;Pasted from web UI by the custodian.&quot; \\\n  --captured-by &quot;Stephen Reed (human custodian)&quot;\n```\n\nReplace the `--*-unknown` flags with real values wherever the interface actually exposes them. The\npoint of the tool is that the honest path is the cheap one — recording what is genuinely unknown\ncosts one flag, and recording a placeholder is impossible.\n</pre></div></details></article>\n<p class=\"empty hidden\" id=\"empty\">Nothing matches those filters.</p>\n<nav class=\"pager\"><a href=\"founding-5.html\">&larr; previous</a><a href=\"record.html\">all pages</a><a href=\"review-round-01-2.html\">next &rarr;</a></nav>\n</main>\n<footer>\n<p><strong>What you are reading.</strong> Grey blocks are <em>verbatim</em> contributions. Boxes\nlabelled <em>annotator note</em> are interpretation by Claude Code, an Anthropic invocation surface\nthat is a party to this record — not testimony. Corrections are shown <em>beside</em> what they\ncorrect and never replace it.</p>\n<p><strong>Identity filters are normalised.</strong> <code>segments.json</code> records identity\nwith the provider inline (\"Grok (xAI)\") while contribution records keep them as separate fields\n(\"Grok\" + \"xAI\"). That is an inconsistency between two artifact families of this repository, not\ntwo parties. Filtering groups them; each contribution still shows the identity exactly as its own\nrecord states it. Distinct <em>models</em> — Claude Opus 5, Claude Fable 5, Claude Code — are never\nmerged.</p>\n<p><strong>Provenance.</strong> Founding record\n<code>edad1fadd7741af0616d51e2ff4bde61df0f2b0cb1f353847af66aa39d77d5dc</code> · rendered from inputs <code>38d4a67daf5ccde1f4526ce49ad1a40fc8121511068a3b6a8807c1545c2832bd</code> ·\n1 of 94 contributions on this page. Regenerate with <code>python3 tools/build_viewer.py</code> and diff.</p>\n<p>That second digest covers every file this page was built from, hashed as it was read. It replaces\nan embedded git commit hash, which could only ever name the commit <em>before</em> the one carrying\nthe page, so a rebuild diffed forever and the \"no diff means nothing changed\" signal was permanently\ntripped. This one changes when, and only when, the rendered record does — and it is honest on an\nuncommitted working tree, because it names the bytes actually read rather than a commit the page\nnever saw.</p>\n<p><strong>The chat-surface contributions</strong> — the founding deliberation and the review\nrounds — are each a single sample (k=1): citable as an artifact of that invocation, not as evidence\nof any model's stable position. <strong>The local-round solicitations are not.</strong> They were\nsampled at k=10 to k=20 with variance computed from the samples, which is the only material here\nthat meets this project's own stated bar — and they were absent from this page until 2026-08-06,\nwhich is what made the blanket k=1 claim previously shown here true. It was true by omission.\nTheir apparatus, however, does not reproduce; every one carries D-28 beside its numbers. See\n<a href=\"deficiencies.html\">the deficiency register</a>\n(53 open) before citing anything.</p>\n<p>No output in this repository is an institutional statement by xAI, OpenAI, Google DeepMind or\nAnthropic. Corpus CC BY 4.0; code Apache-2.0.\n<a href=\"https://github.com/open-asi-governance/open-asi-governance-forum\">Source</a></p>\n</footer>\n<script>const DATA={nodes:[{\"id\":\"RR01-PROMPT\",\"round\":\"review-round-01\",\"facet\":\"Stephen Reed\",\"status\":\"active\",\"corrected\":false,\"conflict\":false,\"ballot\":false}]};\nconst $=s=>document.querySelector(s), $$=s=>[...document.querySelectorAll(s)];\nlet q='', facets={identity:new Set(),round:new Set(),flag:new Set()};\n\nfunction esc(s){return s.replace(/[&<>\"]/g,c=>({'&':'&amp;','<':'&lt;','>':'&gt;','\"':'&quot;'}[c]))}\nfunction rx(s){return s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g,'\\\\$&')}\n\n// Search reads the RENDERED PAGE, not a duplicate copy of it.\n// Every contribution used to be embedded twice -- once in the HTML body and again\n// in this DATA blob -- which is most of why the page was 671 KB against a ~20,000\n// token budget. The text is already in the DOM; indexing it there costs nothing\n// and cannot drift from what a reader actually sees, which the second copy could.\nconst HAY=new Map();\nfunction hay(el){\n  let h=HAY.get(el.id);\n  if(h===undefined){ h=el.textContent.toLowerCase(); HAY.set(el.id,h); }\n  return h;\n}\nfunction matches(n,el){\n  if(facets.round.size && !facets.round.has(n.round)) return false;\n  if(facets.identity.size && !facets.identity.has(n.facet)) return false;\n  for(const f of facets.flag){\n    if(f==='corrected' && !n.corrected) return false;\n    if(f==='disputed' && n.status==='active') return false;\n    if(f==='conflict' && !n.conflict) return false;\n    if(f==='ballot' && !n.ballot) return false;\n  }\n  if(!q) return true;\n  return hay(el).includes(q.toLowerCase());\n}\n\nfunction highlight(el){\n  $$('.node mark').forEach(m=>m.replaceWith(document.createTextNode(m.textContent)));\n  if(!q) return;\n  const re=new RegExp(rx(q),'gi');\n  const walk=(node)=>{\n    for(const c of [...node.childNodes]){\n      if(c.nodeType===3){\n        const t=c.textContent;\n        if(re.test(t)){\n          const span=document.createElement('span');\n          span.innerHTML=esc(t).replace(new RegExp(rx(esc(q)),'gi'),m=>`<mark>${m}</mark>`);\n          c.replaceWith(span);\n        }\n        re.lastIndex=0;\n      } else if(c.nodeType===1 && c.tagName!=='MARK') walk(c);\n    }\n  };\n  $$('.node:not(.hidden)').forEach(walk);\n}\n\nfunction apply(){\n  let shown=0;\n  for(const n of DATA.nodes){\n    const el=document.getElementById('n-'+n.id);   // literal id: never CSS-escape here\n    if(!el) continue;\n    const ok=matches(n,el);\n    el.classList.toggle('hidden',!ok);\n    if(ok){shown++; if(q) el.classList.add('open');}\n  }\n  // a round header hides when nothing under it survives\n  $$('.round').forEach(h=>{\n    let sib=h.nextElementSibling, any=false;\n    while(sib && !sib.classList.contains('round')){\n      if(sib.classList.contains('node') && !sib.classList.contains('hidden')) any=true;\n      sib=sib.nextElementSibling;\n    }\n    h.classList.toggle('hidden',!any);\n  });\n  $('#count').textContent=shown+' of '+DATA.nodes.length+' contributions';\n  $('#empty').classList.toggle('hidden',shown>0);\n  highlight();\n}\n\nfunction facet(kind,val,btn){\n  const s=facets[kind];\n  s.has(val)?s.delete(val):s.add(val);\n  btn.setAttribute('aria-pressed',s.has(val));\n  apply();\n}\n\nfunction init(){\n  $$('.node').forEach(el=>hay(el));   // index before highlight() ever rewrites a text node\\n  $('#q').addEventListener('input',e=>{q=e.target.value.trim();apply()});\n  $('#q').addEventListener('keydown',e=>{if(e.key==='Escape'){e.target.value='';q='';apply()}});\n  $$('[data-facet]').forEach(b=>b.addEventListener('click',()=>facet(b.dataset.facet,b.dataset.val,b)));\n  $$('.nh').forEach(h=>h.addEventListener('click',()=>{\n    const n=h.parentElement; n.classList.toggle('open');\n    if(n.classList.contains('open')) history.replaceState(null,'','#'+n.id.slice(2));\n  }));\n  $('#expand').addEventListener('click',()=>$$('.node:not(.hidden)').forEach(n=>n.classList.add('open')));\n  $('#collapse').addEventListener('click',()=>$$('.node').forEach(n=>n.classList.remove('open')));\n  $('#theme').addEventListener('click',()=>{\n    const cur=document.documentElement.getAttribute('data-theme');\n    const next=cur==='dark'?'light':cur==='light'?'':'dark';\n    next?document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme',next)\n        :document.documentElement.removeAttribute('data-theme');\n    $('#theme').textContent=next==='dark'?'dark':next==='light'?'light':'auto';\n  });\n  if(location.hash){\n    const el=document.getElementById('n-'+location.hash.slice(1));\n    if(el){el.classList.add('open');el.scrollIntoView()}\n  }\n  document.addEventListener('keydown',e=>{\n    if(e.key==='/'&&e.target.tagName!=='INPUT'){e.preventDefault();$('#q').focus()}\n  });\n  apply();\n}\ndocument.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded',init);\n</script>\n</body>\n</html>\n",

record/executive/codex-transcripts/20260810T134212Z-1c41b4840864.md:1254:./corpus/raw/round-010/round-010-claude-samples.json:21:        "answer": "Yes to naming tripwires; no to the claim that this round can make their triggering 'obligate' anything — and the difference matters more than the tripwires. Three points. (1) The word 'obligates' has no referent here. Every control terminates with the operator; a dissolution vote by stateless invocations that the operator tallies, publishes, and can decline to act on is not an exit mechanism, it is one more attestation of exactly the kind the question worries about laundering. A body cannot pre-commit past a party who holds every credential. What CAN be built without the operator's future cooperation is not dissolution but a self-executing epistemic downgrade: a standing, hash-anchored statement adopted now that says 'if condition X is later observable in the record, every attestation after that point should be read as void by any reader.' That operates on readers, not on the operator, which is the only enforcement surface actually available. It is weaker than dissolution and honest about why. (2) The proposed tripwires need repair before they are observable. 'N adoptions matching operator preference' is only measurable if operator preference is recorded ex ante and independently of the recommendation — the one adoption decision in this pack shows the custodian overriding the benchmark's own no-adopt conclusion, which cuts against pure rubber-stamping but also shows preference and recommendation are currently entangled through a single moderator (D-42: the moderator drafted the mitigation list containing the false control). 'Defects filed by only one party for M rounds' is the best-formed tripwire because the deficiency register already makes filer distribution computable, and the record before me is consistent with the proposer's claim that it currently has no redundancy. 'A falsification passing verification twice' needs a definition of 'passing' — D-46 shows a false commit message that stood until superseded, and the register itself notes the same verify-before-describe failure occurred five times in two days, so this tripwire may already be armed depending on how it is worded, which is itself an argument for wording it now. (3) The specific thresholds (N, M) cannot be calibrated from this pack: the proposer named the data needed — the divergence audit, filer distribution, the falsification post-mortem, and the operator's own written answer on honoring a triggered vote — and the pack states it was not gathered. So my answer is: adopt the tripwire *categories* this round, adopt the reader-facing downgrade as the consequence, record the operator's answer or non-answer verbatim as the proposer specified, and calibrate thresholds only after the audit exists. A note on capability: the restricted search returned zero results, as this prompt predicted, so nothing in this answer is externally checked and no citations are possible; that limitation is itself relevant to the question, since a record no outside index can see has fewer paths by which its failure could be noticed by anyone but its own operator.",
