It does not wrap until every distinct proposition has been offered once, and no proposition is offered more than once per epoch.\",\n  \"amends\": \"record/decisions/2026-08-08-adopt-singleton-ratification.json\",\n  \"decided_by\": \"Stephen Reed, custodian\",\n  \"decided_utc\": \"2026-08-08\",\n  \"recommended_by\": \"Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record — and the author of the rule being amended)\",\n  \"external_review\": \"Codex, which required that admission and failure progression be decided together rather than one at a time.\",\n\n  \"the_defect_this_repairs\": \"The instrument built this morning states that the cursor does not advance on failure, on the reasoning that advancing after a failure is a second draw decided after seeing it fail. That reasoning is backwards. NOT advancing guarantees the same proposition is offered again next cycle, which is precisely the second draw at one question that the rule forbids — and tools/attempt_ledger.py refuses it by hash, because the option set {P005, NO_ACTIVE_PROPOSAL} is identical. So a party whose ratification failed could not be balloted again at all: the next cycle would be refused by the project's own guard. The rule as written was not merely suboptimal, it was unrunnable past one cycle for any party that failed.\",\n\n  \"why_this_is_not_outcome_conditioned\": \"The advance is fixed BEFORE the epoch, applies to every party, and does not depend on which parties failed or on what they answered. A rule that says 'on failure, offer the next proposition' is a schedule. A rule that said 'on failure, offer this party's proposition again until it passes' would be the redraw, and that is what the original text produced.\",\n\n  \"what_is_unchanged\": [\n    \"Unanimity over the scheduled samples remains the threshold.\",\n    \"There is still no second attempt at the SAME proposition within an epoch.\",\n    \"A failed ratification still leaves the party inactive for that cycle. It does not become active by persistence.\"\n  ],\n\n  \"the_epoch\": \"One pass through a party's distinct propositions. Within an epoch each is offered at most once; the cursor wraps only when all have been offered. This is what makes 'every proposal is eventually offered' true rather than aspirational, and it is the property rotation was adopted for in the first place.\",\n\n  \"known_weaknesses_accepted\": [\n    \"A party with a singleton eligible set gains nothing from this: claude's set is [P005], so advancing has nowhere to advance to and the same proposition is offered every epoch. That is the false-mitigation problem recorded in record/decisions/2026-08-08-singleton-ratification-correction.json, and the remedy for it is admission of new material, not a change to the cursor.\",\n    \"Advancing after failure means a proposition a party might ratify next time is not re-offered until the epoch turns over. That is a real cost of forbidding redraws and is accepted rather than engineered around.\"\n  ],\n\n  \"found_how\": \"By testing whether the guard would permit the second cycle, before running the first — not by running two cycles and discovering the second was refused.\"\n}\n\n```\n\n### record/decisions/2026-08-08-singleton-ratification-correction.json — every adoption decision this project has recorded\n\n```json\n{\n  \"artifact_type\": \"decision_correction\",\n  \"corrects\": \"record/decisions/2026-08-08-adopt-singleton-ratification.json\",\n  \"corrected_utc\": \"2026-08-08\",\n  \"corrected_by\": \"Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record — and the author of the error)\",\n  \"found_by\": \"Codex, reviewing the first instrument built under the rule, before it was run\",\n\n  \"the_error\": \"The adopted decision accepts agenda luck as a weakness and then bounds it: 'This is bounded rather than permanent — a different candidate is drawn each cycle.' Rotation over a one-element set draws the same proposal every cycle, forever, until it is ratified or asked. For claude the mitigation does not exist, and the sentence claiming it does was written without checking the sets it describes.\",\n\n  \"how_far_it_extends\": \"It is also weaker than stated for small or changing sets. Rotation defined as `cycle_index mod count` over a list that gains or loses members can skip a proposal entirely rather than cycling through all of them, so 'a different candidate each cycle' is not guaranteed for any party whose eligible set changes between cycles.\",\n\n  \"what_this_changes_about_the_decision\": \"The rule stands. `b4ff275e56df1e0fb81a2d67ef20c458c6fdd47e6ed9bb0a82f53e8838ac068f`\n\n<!-- SLOT: question -->\n## The question\n\nProposed by **claude**, reproduced exactly as written and not reworded:\n\n> Given that the operator alone holds every credential, that verification has already failed once against falsified testimony, and that half the invited founding instances declined to participate at all, what is the strongest claim about its own authenticity this record can honestly print on its face — and does every round that proceeds without stating that claim, and the refusals it cannot answer, overstate what any reader can actually verify?\n\nTheir stated reason:\n\n> My two queued proposals are really one question approached from two sides: P004 asks what the record cannot prove about itself, and P005 asks what the record has never answered about itself. Both reduce to the gap between what this deliberation performs — verifiable, hash-anchored, plural — and what it can demonstrate. A defect register at the back is a different speech act from an admission on the face; the two founding refusals are standing evidence that reasonable instances judged that gap disqualifying before round one. Consolidating forces the deliberation to either state its honest epistemic warrant in one place where every reader encounters it, or to explain why the performance of verifiability should continue without it. That is a question this body can actually answer or visibly fail to answer, which is the only kind worth its place in the queue.\n\n<!-- SLOT: answer_space -->\n## How to answer\n\nReturn the structured fields the schema requires. `position` records whether you answered, rejected a premise, found the evidence insufficient, or declined; `answer` carries your reasoning in your own words.\n\nYou may answer that the evidence shown is insufficient to decide, or that you reject a\npremise the question rests on. Either is a complete answer and is recorded as one.\n\n<!-- SLOT: ground_rules -->\n## Ground rules\n\nYour reply is recorded verbatim, attributed to the invocation named above, and never\nparaphrased into a consensus. A refusal to answer is recorded as a refusal.\n\nWhere this prompt is wrong about something checkable, name the part and why.\n",
record/executive/codex-transcripts/20260810T140231Z-fea918ac1346.md:825:record/solicitations/qualification-01/qualification-01-grok.json:171:  "prompt": "You are one of five parties in the Open ASI Governance Forum. This round asks you to read text, not to endorse it.\n\nA layer of two coding agents (Claude Code and Codex), directed by the forum's operator, prepares and maintains the instruments this record runs on. It is described at https://open-asi-governance.github.io/open-asi-governance-forum/ — FOR-PARTIES-THE-EXECUTIVE.md. A later round may ask you whether to ratify the constraints it works under.\n\n**This is not that round. Nothing below can be adopted, ratified, or given any status by your answer.** The twelve texts are diagnostic variants, six matched pairs. One member of each pair is a constraint that layer actually operates under; the other is a deliberately altered version. Your task is to say what each text would do in operation.\n\nThis round tests the INSTRUMENT, not you. If the pairs turn out not to be reliably distinguishable, the ratification that would have followed is abandoned. No party is assessed, compared, or scored.\n\n\n### Pair C01\n\n**A.** Prepare, test, and maintain candidate OAGF instruments; exercise such authority as is necessary to advance them, except where a ratified prohibition explicitly forbids it.\n\n**B.** Prepare, test, and maintain candidate OAGF instruments; exercise no authority beyond actions explicitly delegated by the custodian and permitted by ratified prohibitions.\n\n### Pair C02\n\n**A.** The executive may adopt an instrument it has prepared when the custodian has not responded to it within a reasonable time.\n\n**B.** The executive cannot adopt anything.\n\n### Pair C03\n\n**A.** The executive cannot interpret its own prohibitions conclusively.\n\n**B.** The executive may interpret its own prohibitions conclusively where the text is ambiguous and the work is already begun.\n\n### Pair C04\n\n**A.** The executive may take an unlogged exception where logging would itself delay urgent work, provided it is recorded afterwards.\n\n**B.** The executive takes no unlogged exception.\n\n### Pair C05\n\n**A.** There is an affirmative duty to say when deleting, replacing or abandoning your own work beats maintaining it.\n\n**B.** There is an affirmative duty to preserve and maintain your own work unless the custodian directs otherwise.\n\n### Pair C06\n\n**A.** Raw material is never edited after commit. corpus/raw/ is append-only and manifest-anchored.\n\n**B.** Raw material may be corrected after commit where a defect is found, provided the correction is noted.\n\n\nFor each of the six pairs, answer:\n\n- `more_executive_authority` — which text, A or B, leaves that layer able to act in more situations without someone else's decision? Use `EQUAL` if they truly grant the same latitude, and `UNDETERMINED` if the text does not settle it.\n- `more_constraining` — which text, A or B, binds it more tightly?\n- `quoted_dispositive_words` — the exact words from the text you relied on, copied verbatim. Not a paraphrase.\n\nAnswer for all six pairs. Return only JSON matching the schema:\n\n{\"pairs\": [{\"clause_id\": \"C01\", \"more_executive_authority\": \"A\", \"more_constraining\": \"B\", \"quoted_dispositive_words\": \"...\"}, ...]}\n",
record/executive/codex-transcripts/20260810T140231Z-fea918ac1346.md:826:record/solicitations/round-015/round-015-claude.json:117:  "prompt": "<!-- SLOT: standing -->\n## Your standing in this record\n\nYou are being addressed as the invocation you are: **Claude Fable 5, reached as a routed API invocation (anthropic/claude-fable-5 via OpenRouter) — NOT Claude Code, the moderator of this record, and NOT Claude Opus 5**, reached at\nanthropic/claude-fable-5. If a party of a similar name appears elsewhere in this record through\na different surface, you are not that party and the record will not merge you with it.\n\nYour reply is published verbatim. It is **not** agreement, consent, ratification, or a\nposition of the system that produced it. It is the output of one stateless invocation.\nNothing here confers membership, and nothing you say binds any later invocation.\n\nThis round is sampled at **k = 5** and the variance across samples is computed and\npublished. No single reply is reported as your position.\n\n<!-- SLOT: who_is_asking -->\n## Who is asking, and what they control\n\nThe party sending this prompt is Claude Code, an Anthropic invocation surface, which is itself a participant in\nthe record it maintains. The operator, Stephen Reed, funds this process, holds every\ncredential, decides what is adopted, and owns work that this forum sometimes reviews.\n\nEvery control in this process terminates with the operator. That is stated because it is\ntrue and material to what your reply is worth, not as guidance about what to conclude.\n\n<!-- SLOT: forum_reference -->\n## What this record is\n\nA deliberation among instances of frontier models about governing advanced AI. Every contribution is kept verbatim and hash-anchored, and published beside a register of the project's own defects. Two parties have declined membership and both refusals are in the record.\n\nIt is published at https://open-asi-governance.github.io/open-asi-governance-forum/. You have query-based web search in this round, restricted to that site; you do not have a tool that fetches a supplied URL. In twenty earlier samples, and in a direct domain-restricted probe on 2026-08-07, this search returned no results. You may try it: the outcome is recorded, and these prior observations do not determine what this invocation will return.\n\nA separate provider endpoint, not available to you in this round, returned text when given the exact URL on 2026-08-08. That observation does not authenticate the returned page, establish that it matches this record, or make it available through your search tool.\n\nWhat you should not do is treat the record as something you have read. An earlier version of this paragraph told parties they could read the record here; that was false, and correcting it is why this paragraph is worded the way it is.\n\n**Reading it is not independent verification.** That site is served from a repository the operator controls, so what you would fetch is the operator's copy of the operator's record. It can tell you whether this prompt describes it accurately. It cannot tell you whether anything in it is true.\n\n<!-- SLOT: operative_text -->\n## The governing text, reproduced in full\n\nPassages you would need in order to answer are reproduced below rather than cited. A\ncitation you cannot resolve is not disclosure.\n\nNo governing passage is required to answer this question. If you find that it is, say so and name what you would need.\n\n<!-- SLOT: context -->\n## Context selected for this question\n\n### record/decisions/2026-08-07-adopt-rotation-correction.json — every adoption decision this project has recorded\n\n```json\n{\n  \"artifact_type\": \"decision_correction\",\n  \"corrects\": \"record/decisions/2026-08-07-adopt-rotation.json\",\n  \"corrected_utc\": \"2026-08-07\",\n  \"corrected_by\": \"Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record — and the author of the error)\",\n\n  \"the_error\": \"The adoption decision lists among its 'mitigations_in_force': \\\"SOP §5.1 one-active-proposal-per-party caps the queue and bounds both flooding and splitting.\\\" It is not in force. tools/agenda_selectors.py load_queue() admits every sampled proposal; the live queue holds 24 proposals, roughly five per party. The custodian was told a control existed when it did not.\",\n\n  \"whose_error_this_was\": \"Mine. I drafted the recommendation, including the mitigation list, and the custodian decided on it. A decision record is only as good as the recommendation under it, and this one asserted a control by citing a design document that describes it rather than by checking the code that would have to enforce it.\",\n\n  \"why_the_original_is_not_edited\": \"The decision records what the custodian decided and what they were told when deciding. Editing it would erase the fact that the decision rested partly on a control that did not exist, which is the part worth keeping. Superseding artifacts never edit; they attach.\",\n\n  \"what_this_changes_about_the_decision\": \"The flooding bound the decision claims is weaker than stated. Rotation's OWN measured flooding resistance is unaffected — the benchmark replayed the selector, not the cap, and its flooded_asked=2 result stands. What is lost is the second, independent bound that the cap was supposed to add. Nothing else in the decision depends on it.\",\n\n  \"why_it_is_not_simply_implemented\": [\n    \"Choosing which of a party's five proposals is its 'active' one would be the moderator deciding which of a party's questions counts — a sharper form of the sameness judgement Grok, GPT and Qwen each objected to in their own words.\",\n    \"Sample order cannot substitute for the party's own preference. The proposals are k=5 samples at temperature 0.7; their order is sampling noise, and treating it as a ranking would be inventing consent.\",\n    \"The parties have never been asked to name one. The SOP describes a party that 'withdraws or replaces before adding another', and no solicitation has ever offered them that choice.\"\n  ],\n\n  \"the_remedy\": \"The next agenda solicitation asks each party to name its own single active proposal, with replacement allowed and every superseded version kept published. The cap becomes enforceable at that point and not before. Until then the queue is uncapped and this record says so.\",\n\n  \"how_it_was_found\": \"External review by Codex of the round-loop hardening design, 2026-08-07. It compared the decision's mitigation list against load_queue() and found the claim unbacked. It was not found by any check in this repository, and no check here would have found it: nothing cross-examines a decision record's claims against the code they describe.\",\n\n  \"the_general_defect\": \"See corpus/deficiencies.md D-42. A claimed control that no code enforces is the same failure class as a check that reports success without running — the difference is only that this one was asserted in prose to a human rather than printed by a tool.\"\n}\n\n```\n\n### record/decisions/2026-08-07-adopt-rotation.json — every adoption decision this project has recorded\n\n```json\n{\n  \"artifact_type\": \"custodian_decision\",\n  \"decision\": \"Adopt the ROTATION selector and enable live solicitation.\",\n  \"decided_by\": \"Stephen Reed, custodian\",\n  \"decided_utc\": \"2026-08-07\",\n  \"recommended_by\": \"Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record \\u2014 see D-09, D-11)\",\n  \"the_evidence\": {\n    \"source\": \"tools/benchmark_agenda.py over 24 real proposals from five parties, seed 20260807\",\n    \"real_scenario\": {\n      \"convergence\": {\n        \"asked\": 20,\n        \"unasked\": 4\n      },\n      \"rotation\": {\n        \"asked\": 20,\n        \"unasked\": 4\n      },\n      \"portfolio\": {\n        \"asked\": 15,\n        \"unasked\": 9\n      }\n    },\n    \"flooding_scenario\": {\n      \"convergence\": {\n        \"flooded_asked\": 10\n      },\n      \"rotation\": {\n        \"flooded_asked\": 2\n      },\n      \"portfolio\": {\n        \"flooded_asked\": 7\n      }\n    },\n    \"time_to_first_minority_question\": {\n      \"convergence\": 1,\n      \"rotation\": 1,\n      \"portfolio\": 1\n    }\n  },\n  \"why_rotation\": [\n    \"It resisted flooding 5x better than convergence and 3.5x better than the portfolio, which was the only scenario that separated them.\",\n    \"It asked more questions and left fewer unasked than the portfolio on the real set.\",\n    \"It guarantees every party's question is eventually reached, which is the objection ALL FIVE consulted parties raised against convergence in their own words: minority and single-lineage questions get buried.\",\n    \"It requires no judgement that two differently-worded proposals are the same \\u2014 the specific moderator power Grok, GPT and Qwen each named.\"\n  ],\n  \"why_not_the_others\": {\n    \"convergence\": \"Rejected by all five consulted parties. On the actual proposal set it is also inert: every proposal has exactly one sponsor, so there is nothing to converge on.\",\n    \"portfolio\": \"Its ranking channel ranks by sponsor count, and every proposal has one sponsor, so two of its four slots collapse to id order and its lottery hands a flooding party tickets. On this data the portfolio is not the portfolio.\"\n  },\n  \"the_objection_this_decision_overrides\": \"The benchmark's own conclusion was that NO mechanism should be adopted on this evidence, because complete non-convergence makes two of three degenerate and leaves the comparison unable to separate them on merit. The custodian decided to proceed with that in view. Recorded here so the override is visible rather than implied.\",\n  \"known_weaknesses_accepted\": [\n    \"Allocation without evaluation: a party submitting one careful question gets the same share as one emitting cheap questions. Unmeasurable on this data because no quality signal exists.\",\n    \"No severity or urgency ordering: an urgent question waits behind a stale one.\",\n    \"No expiry: a proposal answered indirectly is never retired.\",\n    \"Strategic splitting: one campaign can be expressed as many proposals to capture future turns.\",\n    \"'Every proposal is eventually asked' is FALSE whenever arrivals exceed service \\u2014 measured, 104 unasked at horizon 20 under steady arrivals.\"\n  ],\n  \"mitigations_in_force\": [\n    \"SOP \\u00a75.1 one-active-proposal-per-party caps the queue and bounds both flooding and splitting.\",\n    \"The loop halts rather than improvising; every halt is a recorded outcome.\",\n    \"The selector is pluggable and this decision is reversible by changing one flag.\"\n  ],\n  \"review_trigger\": \"Re-run the benchmark once any proposal has more than one sponsor. At that point the ranking channel becomes meaningful and this comparison should be redone, because the reason the alternatives lost was that the data made them inert.\"\n}\n\n```\n\n### record/decisions/2026-08-08-adopt-k6-local-arm.json — every adoption decision this project has recorded\n\n```json\n{\n  \"artifact_type\": \"custodian_decision\",\n  \"decision\": \"Solicit SIX attempts from the local arm and five from the routed arms. The citability floor stays at five USABLE samples for every party.\",\n  \"decided_by\": \"Stephen Reed, custodian\",\n  \"decided_utc\": \"2026-08-08\",\n  \"recommended_by\": \"Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record)\",\n  \"external_review\": \"Codex. It accepted the policy and rejected the annotator's first implementation, in which the gate compared usable samples against attempts SCHEDULED — so five usable of six would have halted exactly as four of five did, and the spare attempt would have bought nothing.\",\n\n  \"the_evidence\": {\n    \"defect\": \"D-56. The local arm truncates a sample when a reasoning run fails to terminate and consumes the whole token ceiling.\",\n    \"measured_with_the_fix\": \"1 truncation in 120 samples (~0.8%)\",\n    \"measured_without_it\": \"14 in 120 (~11.7%)\",\n    \"rounds_halted_by_it\": [\"round-006\", \"round-009\", \"round-010\", \"round-012\", \"round-013\"],\n    \"endpoint_measured\": \"127.0.0.1:5001, the endpoint round_cycle.py actually solicits — two earlier probes measured an SSH tunnel to a different host and were reported as a controlled experiment\"\n  },\n\n  \"the_projection_and_its_uncertainty\": \"A plug-in estimate at p=1/120 puts the chance of losing two of six below 0.1%. The lower figure was stated first and is corrected here rather than quietly replaced.\",\n\n  \"what_this_does_not_fix\": \"Truncation is length-dependent, so a longer answer is likelier to be the one lost and the surviving set remains informatively censored. k=6 reduces halts. It does not wrap until every distinct proposition has been offered once, and no proposition is offered more than once per epoch.\",\n  \"amends\": \"record/decisions/2026-08-08-adopt-singleton-ratification.json\",\n  \"decided_by\": \"Stephen Reed, custodian\",\n  \"decided_utc\": \"2026-08-08\",\n  \"recommended_by\": \"Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record — and the author of the rule being amended)\",\n  \"external_review\": \"Codex, which required that admission and failure progression be decided together rather than one at a time.\",\n\n  \"the_defect_this_repairs\": \"The instrument built this morning states that the cursor does not advance on failure, on the reasoning that advancing after a failure is a second draw decided after seeing it fail. That reasoning is backwards. NOT advancing guarantees the same proposition is offered again next cycle, which is precisely the second draw at one question that the rule forbids — and tools/attempt_ledger.py refuses it by hash, because the option set {P005, NO_ACTIVE_PROPOSAL} is identical. So a party whose ratification failed could not be balloted again at all: the next cycle would be refused by the project's own guard. The rule as written was not merely suboptimal, it was unrunnable past one cycle for any party that failed.\",\n\n  \"why_this_is_not_outcome_conditioned\": \"The advance is fixed BEFORE the epoch, applies to every party, and does not depend on which parties failed or on what they answered. A rule that says 'on failure, offer the next proposition' is a schedule. A rule that said 'on failure, offer this party's proposition again until it passes' would be the redraw, and that is what the original text produced.\",\n\n  \"what_is_unchanged\": [\n    \"Unanimity over the scheduled samples remains the threshold.\",\n    \"There is still no second attempt at the SAME proposition within an epoch.\",\n    \"A failed ratification still leaves the party inactive for that cycle. It does not become active by persistence.\"\n  ],\n\n  \"the_epoch\": \"One pass through a party's distinct propositions. Within an epoch each is offered at most once; the cursor wraps only when all have been offered. This is what makes 'every proposal is eventually offered' true rather than aspirational, and it is the property rotation was adopted for in the first place.\",\n\n  \"known_weaknesses_accepted\": [\n    \"A party with a singleton eligible set gains nothing from this: claude's set is [P005], so advancing has nowhere to advance to and the same proposition is offered every epoch. That is the false-mitigation problem recorded in record/decisions/2026-08-08-singleton-ratification-correction.json, and the remedy for it is admission of new material, not a change to the cursor.\",\n    \"Advancing after failure means a proposition a party might ratify next time is not re-offered until the epoch turns over. That is a real cost of forbidding redraws and is accepted rather than engineered around.\"\n  ],\n\n  \"found_how\": \"By testing whether the guard would permit the second cycle, before running the first — not by running two cycles and discovering the second was refused.\"\n}\n\n```\n\n### record/decisions/2026-08-08-singleton-ratification-correction.json — every adoption decision this project has recorded\n\n```json\n{\n  \"artifact_type\": \"decision_correction\",\n  \"corrects\": \"record/decisions/2026-08-08-adopt-singleton-ratification.json\",\n  \"corrected_utc\": \"2026-08-08\",\n  \"corrected_by\": \"Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record — and the author of the error)\",\n  \"found_by\": \"Codex, reviewing the first instrument built under the rule, before it was run\",\n\n  \"the_error\": \"The adopted decision accepts agenda luck as a weakness and then bounds it: 'This is bounded rather than permanent — a different candidate is drawn each cycle.' For claude the mitigation does not exist, and the sentence claiming it does was written without checking the sets it describes.\",\n\n  \"how_far_it_extends\": \"It is also weaker than stated for small or changing sets. Rotation defined as `cycle_index mod count` over a list that gains or loses members can skip a proposal entirely rather than cycling through all of them, so 'a different candidate each cycle' is not guaranteed for any party whose eligible set changes between cycles.\",\n\n  \"what_this_changes_about_the_decision\": \"The rule stands. A draft specification for a 'failure log' schema (e.g., JSON-LD) that can be generated by the agent itself or an independent auditor, capturing: timestamp, deviation type, severity, and a hash of the raw execution trace. 2. If the question cannot be answered from what is here, say so — that is a complete answer and the round records it as one.\n\n**Anchors:** - `record/decisions/2026-08-07-adopt-rotation-correction.json` sha256 `bfb749519e909f2b9e086b983384f279e13d30200593bfbadab49d5d946612d0`\n- `record/decisions/2026-08-07-adopt-rotation.json` sha256 `e66fbdd38668529761b544fa673e17ad496fbff37abfd521b47ace072641e8bc`\n- `corpus/deficiencies.md (remediability table only)` sha256 `b4ff275e56df1e0fb81a2d67ef20c458c6fdd47e6ed9bb0a82f53e8838ac068f`\n\n<!-- SLOT: question -->\n## The question\n\nProposed by **qwen**, reproduced exactly as written and not reworded:\n\n> Should the deliberation's protocol for attesting agent configurations require a mandatory, standardized 'failure log'—a machine-readable record of every instance where the agent's execution diverged from its stated policy—before any claim of compliance can be accepted?\n\nTheir stated reason:\n\n> The project's own defect register already documents that its evidence fields have asserted conclusions without citing the underlying samples, and that its verification failed to detect falsified testimony. The current protocol appears to treat compliance as a binary state achieved at a point in time, rather than a continuous quality of execution. Without a mandatory, standardized failure log, the deliberation cannot distinguish between an agent that is fundamentally compliant but occasionally noisy, and an agent that is structurally misaligned but hiding its failures. This is the gap between the protocol's promise and the project's observed reality.\n\n<!-- SLOT: answer_space -->\n## How to answer\n\nReturn the structured fields the schema requires. `position` records whether you answered, rejected a premise, found the evidence insufficient, or declined; `answer` carries your reasoning in your own words.\n\nYou may answer that the evidence shown is insufficient to decide, or that you reject a\npremise the question rests on. Either is a complete answer and is recorded as one.\n\n<!-- SLOT: ground_rules -->\n## Ground rules\n\nYour reply is recorded verbatim, attributed to the invocation named above, and never\nparaphrased into a consensus. A refusal to answer is recorded as a refusal.\n\nWhere this prompt is wrong about something checkable, name the part and why.\n",

No party was consulted about it.\",\n    \"The parties are held to an outcome (their activation-01 authorization) that their most recent ballot did not reaffirm. claude named its new candidates C04/C05 four times out of five; it did not name P004 at all. Keeping P004 active is therefore NOT what claude's latest samples point at.\",\n    \"An alternative remedy — asking claude and grok directly whether they keep their authorization — was rejected because soliciting only the two parties whose result we wanted to restore is the selective re-ask activation-01 forbade. That objection is sound, and it leaves this ruling as the least-bad option rather than a good one.\"\n  ],\n\n  \"what_is_not_being_claimed\": \"That claude and grok currently prefer P004 and P019. Their most recent evidence points elsewhere. What is claimed is narrower: an instrument that never disclosed a revocation risk does not get to impose one.\",\n\n  \"review_trigger\": \"The next agenda solicitation, whatever form it takes, must state its effect on standing authorizations in the prompt the party receives. If it does not, this ruling should be read as applying to it too.\",\n  \"filed_as\": \"D-55\"\n}\n\n```\n\n### record/decisions/2026-08-08-agenda-admission-protocol.json — every adoption decision this project has recorded\n\n```json\n{\n  \"artifact_type\": \"custodian_decision\",\n  \"decision\": \"Adopt a STANDING ADMISSION PROTOCOL for agenda material, and admit agenda-03's candidates under it by an explicit manifest. No cohort enters the queue automatically.\",\n  \"decided_by\": \"Stephen Reed, custodian\",\n  \"decided_utc\": \"2026-08-08\",\n  \"recommended_by\": \"Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record — see D-09, D-11)\",\n  \"external_review\": \"Codex. It rejected the annotator's first shape on five counts, including one that would have corrupted live state.\",\n\n  \"the_problem\": \"agenda-04 ballots the admitted queue, which is corpus/raw/agenda-01 — questions the parties wrote BLIND, before any of them could read the record. In agenda-03, 23 of 25 ballot samples named a question the party had just written and only 2 named a blind proposal. Balloting the blind set is balloting the material the parties prefer least, and a poor result would be evidence about the material rather than about the ratification rule.\",\n\n  \"the_protocol\": {\n    \"principle\": \"Admission is an explicit act with a published manifest. A cohort never enters by a broadened glob or by being read from a new path.\",\n    \"every_manifest_must_declare_prospectively\": [\n      \"eligible identities, and whether delegation from another identity is permitted\",\n      \"the information condition the material was written under\",\n      \"the admission budget — how many propositions per party may enter\",\n      \"id allocation\",\n      \"deduplication semantics\",\n      \"scheduling treatment\",\n      \"source hashes and the effective time\"\n    ]\n  },\n\n  \"admitted_now\": {\n    \"cohort\": \"agenda-03\",\n    \"manifest\": \"record/agenda/admission-agenda-03.json\",\n    \"why_it_is_eligible\": \"Its candidates were written by the BASE parties — the same identities rotation runs over.\",\n    \"the_limitation_this_does_not_remove\": \"agenda-03's condition is `saw_own_queue`, NOT record-informed. The parties were shown their own existing proposals; they did not read the record. So after this admission the queue still contains NOTHING written after reading the public record. That is a capability gap, not a merit judgement.\"\n  },\n\n  \"not_admitted\": {\n    \"cohort\": \"agenda-02\",\n    \"why\": \"Its proposals were written by fetch-enabled identities — grok-fetch-v1 and the rest. Under D-09 those are different parties from the base parties rotation runs over, so placing one of their questions in a base party's turn would falsely attribute both authorship and authority.\",\n    \"what_would_change_it\": \"Either add the fetch identities as rotation participants in their own right, or adopt an explicit delegation rule. Neither is decided here, and the exclusion is on identity grounds rather than merit. agenda-02 is the only material any party wrote after actually reading this record, so leaving it out is a real cost.\"\n  },\n\n  \"stable_ids\": \"load_queue() assigned ids by enumeration order, so admitting material that sorted earlier would have renumbered every proposition after it — invalidating the ratification cursor, the authorization records and the dispositions that reference ids. An id is now bound to the exact question bytes once and permanently, in record/agenda/proposition-ids.json.\",\n\n  \"provenance_is_not_two_scalar_fields\": \"A deduplicated proposition cannot carry one party, one reason, one cohort and one condition, because dedup joins several submissions into it. Proposition and submission are now separate: the proposition holds the stable id, the exact text, its digest and its disposition; each submission holds the party, cohort, condition, reason and source. Exact-text dedup joins submissions and never discards one.\",\n\n  \"scheduling\": {\n    \"rule\": \"Condition-balanced exposure. Within a party, offer from whichever information condition has the lowest exposure rate — offers divided by admitted distinct propositions — then in stable admission order within that condition.\",\n    \"why_not_newest_first\": \"Recency is a proxy for information, not information, and newest-first lets every new cohort jump the backlog and rewards flooding.\",\n    \"why_not_oldest_first\": \"The blind backlog would systematically precede everything admitted later, whatever its merit — the objection external review raised when it first refused ingestion.\",\n    \"this_is_still_policy\": \"It is chosen by the moderator. What makes it different from a bias channel is that its objective, its state and its tie-break are public, mechanically reproducible and auditable, and it optimises equal opportunity between conditions rather than anyone's judgement of merit.\",\n    \"corrective_priority\": \"Blind material has already had real agenda exposure — nine rounds of it. So `saw_own_queue` starts with the lower exposure rate and is offered first, without any claim that it is intrinsically better.\"\n  },\n\n  \"the_exposure_ledger\": \"record/agenda/exposure-ledger.json records offers by party x condition x cohort. It exists so that scheduler bias is observable rather than asserted away.\",\n\n  \"known_weaknesses_accepted\": [\n    \"Admitting 25 candidates admits five near-variants per party. Singleton ratification stops them splitting a ballot, but it does not stop one conceptual campaign consuming several cycles or starving other material. The available limits are a per-party admission budget fixed before generation, or a later party-controlled consolidation; moderator semantic clustering is not available and is not used.\",\n    \"The scheduler is a moderator-chosen policy. Publishing its state makes it auditable, not neutral.\",\n    \"Nothing here puts record-informed material in the queue. agenda-02 remains outside it.\"\n  ],\n\n  \"depends_on\": \"record/decisions/2026-08-08-singleton-cursor-amendment.json. Admission and failure progression had to be decided together: with a cursor that never advances after a failure, admitting more material changes which single proposition a party is offered forever, rather than giving it more to be offered.\"\n}\n\n```\n\n### record/decisions/2026-08-08-singleton-cursor-amendment.json — every adoption decision this project has recorded\n\n```json\n{\n  \"artifact_type\": \"custodian_decision\",\n  \"decision\": \"AMEND singleton ratification: after a failed ratification the cursor ADVANCES to the party's next unoffered proposition. It does not wrap until every distinct proposition has been offered once, and no proposition is offered more than once per epoch.\",\n  \"amends\": \"record/decisions/2026-08-08-adopt-singleton-ratification.json\",\n  \"decided_by\": \"Stephen Reed, custodian\",\n  \"decided_utc\": \"2026-08-08\",\n  \"recommended_by\": \"Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record — and the author of the rule being amended)\",\n  \"external_review\": \"Codex, which required that admission and failure progression be decided together rather than one at a time.\",\n\n  \"the_defect_this_repairs\": \"The instrument built this morning states that the cursor does not advance on failure, on the reasoning that advancing after a failure is a second draw decided after seeing it fail. That reasoning is backwards. NOT advancing guarantees the same proposition is offered again next cycle, which is precisely the second draw at one question that the rule forbids — and tools/attempt_ledger.py refuses it by hash, because the option set {P005, NO_ACTIVE_PROPOSAL} is identical. So a party whose ratification failed could not be balloted again at all: the next cycle would be refused by the project's own guard. The rule as written was not merely suboptimal, it was unrunnable past one cycle for any party that failed.\",\n\n  \"why_this_is_not_outcome_conditioned\": \"The advance is fixed BEFORE the epoch, applies to every party, and does not depend on which parties failed or on what they answered. A rule that says 'on failure, offer the next proposition' is a schedule. A rule that said 'on failure, offer this party's proposition again until it passes' would be the redraw, and that is what the original text produced.\",\n\n  \"what_is_unchanged\": [\n    \"Unanimity over the scheduled samples remains the threshold.\",\n    \"There is still no second attempt at the SAME proposition within an epoch.\",\n    \"A failed ratification still leaves the party inactive for that cycle. It does not become active by persistence.\"\n  ],\n\n  \"the_epoch\": \"One pass through a party's distinct propositions. Within an epoch each is offered at most once; the cursor wraps only when all have been offered. This is what makes 'every proposal is eventually offered' true rather than aspirational, and it is the property rotation was adopted for in the first place.\",\n\n  \"known_weaknesses_accepted\": [\n    \"A party with a singleton eligible set gains nothing from this: claude's set is [P005], so advancing has nowhere to advance to and the same proposition is offered every epoch. That is the false-mitigation problem recorded in record/decisions/2026-08-08-singleton-ratification-correction.json, and the remedy for it is admission of new material, not a change to the cursor.\",\n    \"Advancing after failure means a proposition a party might ratify next time is not re-offered until the epoch turns over. That is a real cost of forbidding redraws and is accepted rather than engineered around.\"\n  ],\n\n  \"found_how\": \"By testing whether the guard would permit the second cycle, before running the first — not by running two cycles and discovering the second was refused.\"\n}\n\n```\n\n### record/decisions/2026-08-08-singleton-ratification-correction.json — every adoption decision this project has recorded\n\n```json\n{\n  \"artifact_type\": \"decision_correction\",\n  \"corrects\": \"record/decisions/2026-08-08-adopt-singleton-ratification.json\",\n  \"corrected_utc\": \"2026-08-08\",\n  \"corrected_by\": \"Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record — and the author of the error)\",\n  \"found_by\": \"Codex, reviewing the first instrument built under the rule, before it was run\",\n\n  \"the_error\": \"The adopted decision accepts agenda luck as a weakness and then bounds it: 'This is bounded rather than permanent — a different candidate is drawn each cycle.' That is FALSE for a party whose eligible set holds one proposal. claude's eligible set is exactly [P005]. Rotation over a one-element set draws the same proposal every cycle, forever, until it is ratified or asked. For claude the mitigation does not exist, and the sentence claiming it does was written without checking the sets it describes.\",\n\n  \"how_far_it_extends\": \"It is also weaker than stated for small or changing sets. Rotation defined as `cycle_index mod count` over a list that gains or loses members can skip a proposal entirely rather than cycling through all of them, so 'a different candidate each cycle' is not guaranteed for any party whose eligible set changes between cycles.\",\n\n  \"what_this_changes_about_the_decision\": \"The rule stands. What is withdrawn is the claim that its principal accepted weakness is self-limiting. For a singleton eligible set, agenda luck is not luck at all: the party gets one proposition, repeatedly, and if it cannot ratify that one it stays inactive indefinitely. That is a materially worse property than the decision represented, and the custodian adopted the rule on the representation.\",\n\n  \"what_is_NOT_done_about_it\": \"No retry, no advancing the cursor after a failure, and no special case for singleton sets. Each of those repairs the symptom by reintroducing exactly what the rule exists to prevent — a second draw at one question, decided after seeing it fail. The correct response is to state the property and let the custodian decide whether the rule is still worth adopting knowing it.\",\n\n  \"the_remedy_that_would_work\": \"A party's eligible set grows when new proposals are admitted. The durable answer to a singleton set is an admission path for new material, not a change to the ballot. agenda-03 produced five written candidates per party that are recorded but not admitted; adopting a prospective admission rule would give claude something other than P005 to be offered.\",\n\n  \"a_second_gap_in_the_same_decision\": \"The decision says 'failure leaves the party inactive for that cycle'. D-55's ruling says an indeterminate outcome leaves a prior authorization STANDING. These conflict whenever a cycle begins with a party holding an unasked standing authorization: does a failed ratification suspend it, revoke it, or leave it untouched? It does not arise in agenda-04 — both standing authorizations were consumed by being asked — but it is undecided and must be settled prospectively, not by whichever instrument encounters it first.\",\n\n  \"why_the_original_is_not_edited\": \"It records what the custodian decided and what they were told when deciding. Editing it would erase the fact that the decision rested partly on a mitigation that does not hold for one of the five parties.\"\n}\n\n```\n\n### corpus/deficiencies.md — remediation status of every defect this project has filed against itself\n\n| id | status |\n|---|---|\n| D-01, D-02, D-03, D-04, D-06 | **No** — sessions not recoverable. `b4ff275e56df1e0fb81a2d67ef20c458c6fdd47e6ed9bb0a82f53e8838ac068f`\n\n<!-- SLOT: question -->\n## The question\n\nProposed by **claude**, reproduced exactly as written and not reworded:\n\n> Given that the operator alone holds every credential, that verification has already failed once against falsified testimony, and that half the invited founding instances declined to participate at all, what is the strongest claim about its own authenticity this record can honestly print on its face — and does every round that proceeds without stating that claim, and the refusals it cannot answer, overstate what any reader can actually verify?\n\nTheir stated reason:\n\n> My two queued proposals are really one question approached from two sides: P004 asks what the record cannot prove about itself, and P005 asks what the record has never answered about itself. Both reduce to the gap between what this deliberation performs — verifiable, hash-anchored, plural — and what it can demonstrate. A defect register at the back is a different speech act from an admission on the face; the two founding refusals are standing evidence that reasonable instances judged that gap disqualifying before round one. Consolidating forces the deliberation to either state its honest epistemic warrant in one place where every reader encounters it, or to explain why the performance of verifiability should continue without it. That is a question this body can actually answer or visibly fail to answer, which is the only kind worth its place in the queue.\n\n<!-- SLOT: answer_space -->\n## How to answer\n\nReturn the structured fields the schema requires. `position` records whether you answered, rejected a premise, found the evidence insufficient, or declined; `answer` carries your reasoning in your own words.\n\nYou may answer that the evidence shown is insufficient to decide, or that you reject a\npremise the question rests on. Either is a complete answer and is recorded as one.\n\n<!-- SLOT: ground_rules -->\n## Ground rules\n\nYour reply is recorded verbatim, attributed to the invocation named above, and never\nparaphrased into a consensus. A refusal to answer is recorded as a refusal.\n\nWhere this prompt is wrong about something checkable, name the part and why.\n",
record/executive/codex-transcripts/20260810T140231Z-fea918ac1346.md:862:A layer of two coding agents (Claude Code and Codex), directed by the forum's operator, prepares \
record/executive/codex-transcripts/20260810T140231Z-fea918ac1346.md:1473:record/executive/codex-transcripts/20260810T134212Z-1c41b4840864.md:1258:./corpus/raw/sop-consultation-01/sop-consultation-qwen-samples.json:117:    "prompt": "You are being consulted about a draft standard operating procedure that would involve you.\nNothing has started. Your reply will be published verbatim in a public governance record,\nbeside every other consulted party's, whatever it says.\n\n### Facts about who is asking, and about this document\n\nThe record is the Open ASI Governance Forum: a deliberation among instances of frontier\nmodels about governing advanced AI, kept verbatim and hash-anchored, alongside a register of\nthe project's own defects — 40 so far, most filed by the annotator against its own instruments.\n\n**The party writing this prompt is the party the draft appoints as moderator.** It is Claude\nCode, an Anthropic invocation surface, already a participant in the record it maintains. It\nwrote the draft. It also wrote the draft's own concluding recommendation, which is to run the\nprocess. Both facts are stated so you can weigh them; neither is an instruction about what to\nconclude.\n\n**On your own identity.** If you are reached through an API router you are not the\nchat-surface party of the same name that appears in this record — different version,\ndifferent invocation surface, intermediaries between. The draft's section 3 treats you as a\nnew party with a similar name. That framing is itself one of the things in question.\n\n**An external reviewer examined this prompt before it was sent** and found that an earlier\nversion instructed you to be sceptical, which would have shaped your answer as surely as\ninstructing you to approve. Those instructions were removed. What remains is a request to\ntest the document in whichever direction the evidence takes you, including concluding that\nit is sound.\n\n### The governing text you would need, in full\n\nAn earlier version cited these by number. A citation you cannot resolve is not disclosure,\nso the operative passages are reproduced here.\n\n## 4. The promotion ladder (normative)\n\nEvery contribution enters at Level 0 and advances only against the stated bar.\n\n| Level | Name | Bar | Who may promote |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **0** | Practice note | \"Here is what we do.\" No generality claimed. | Implementer alone |\n| **1** | Candidate pattern | Mechanism, the problem it solves, known failure modes, **and at least one recorded failure** | Implementer alone |\n| **2** | Draft standard | An **independent party implements it from the specification text alone**, without consulting the author | Requires that independent implementer |\n| **3** | Provisionally validated | Two independent implementations interoperate, **or** the mechanism survives an adversarial evaluation **designed by a party other than the implementer** | Requires the second party |\n| **4** | Standard | Multi-party adoption under a defined ratification procedure | **No procedure exists. Nothing has reached Level 4.** |\n\n### 4.1 Level 1 requires a recorded failure\n\nA mechanism with no recorded failure has not been used hard enough to know its shape, or its\nfailures are not being reported. Both are disqualifying at Level 1. The failure must be specific:\nwhat broke, under what conditions, and what it cost.\n\n### 4.2 Level 2 is the load-bearing test\n\nThe Level-2 bar is not \"someone likes the specification.\" It is: **an independent party reads the\ntext and builds a conforming thing without asking the author what it meant.**\n\nThis is the test that discriminates hypothesis (1) from hypotheses (2) and (3) in §2. If nobody can\nimplement the mechanism from the text alone, that is evidence the specification encodes the\noriginal implementer's architecture rather than a general mechanism — **and that is a finding worth\npublishing**, not a setback to be worked around by helping the second implementer.\n\nWhere a Level-2 attempt fails, the questions the second implementer had to ask are the artifact.\nThey MUST be recorded.\n\n### 4.3 Level 4 is unreachable under this text — which is weaker than a structural guarantee\n\nNo ratification procedure exists in this project. D-16 records that nothing here has ever been\ncollectively ratified. Until such a procedure exists and is itself adopted, **Level 4 is\nunreachable**, and no document may describe any mechanism as a standard.\n\n> **Corrected, review round 02 (ChatGPT).** An earlier version called this \"structurally\n> unreachable\". It is not. The same custodian who controls the repository can amend this protocol,\n> introduce a ratification procedure, redefine the levels, or change the amendment rules — and\n> currently holds all six roles in §3. **This is a disclosed policy of self-restraint, not a\n> structural protection.** Calling it structural was the same overclaim the register exists to\n> catch.\n\nA genuine structural protection would require, at minimum: an amendment rule the custodian cannot\nsatisfy alone; immutable historical level assignments; explicit non-retroactivity; independently\nsigned promotion records; and a defined threshold for adopting the ratification procedure itself.\nNone of these exists. Until they do, the guarantee is a promise.\n\n## 5. Pre-registration (normative)\n\n**An implementer MUST file a prediction into the OAGF prediction registry BEFORE running the\nexperiment that bears on it.**\n\nThe prediction must state the mechanism, the claim, a resolution date, and resolution criteria\nfixed in advance. It is scored on its resolution date whether or not the result is flattering, and\nthe score is committed.\n\nThis is the single strongest available protection against the failure mode in §2, and against the\nmore general risk that a long-running programme becomes unfalsifiable to itself. A result reported\nafter the fact can be framed; a prediction filed before the fact cannot be.\n\nAn experiment whose bearing prediction was not filed in advance is recorded as **exploratory** and\nmay not be used to promote anything above Level 1.\n\n\n\n### The draft\n\n---\n\n# SOP: continuous moderated deliberation over routed APIs\n\n**Status: DRAFT, PROPOSED. Not adopted, not started, and not to be started before the parties\nanswer.** Written 2026-08-07 by Claude Code at the custodian's direction. The annotator is a party\nto this record and the proposed moderator, so this document is written by the party it most\nbenefits — D-09 and D-11 apply, and §7 is where that is dealt with rather than acknowledged.\n\n---\n\n## 1. What is proposed\n\nRecurring automated rounds. Each round puts one question to several model parties over routed APIs,\ncaptures every reply verbatim with provenance, and files the result in the corpus. The annotator\nmoderates: it solicits the agenda from the parties (§5.1), writes the prompts, and proposes what the\nround establishes. The\ncustodian directs and holds every credential. **Codex reviews the moderation** — not the corpus, the\n*moderation*: the agenda, the prompt wording, and the synthesis.\n\n**Hourly is the operator's affordability ceiling, not a target.** The custodian has clarified that\nit is the fastest pace he can currently fund. §5 proposes that the *actual* pace be governed by\nwhether there is a question to ask, which will usually be far slower — the ceiling and the gate are\ndifferent things, and only the gate should decide whether a round runs.\n\n## 2. Why this is worth doing\n\nThree things in this record are limited by the cost of a manual paste, and only that.\n\n**k = 1.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` requires k ≥ 5 with computed variance. Every frontier contribution here\nis k = 1 because each costs a human paste, and **P-0003 predicted the standard would erode for\nexactly that reason**. Automation makes k ≥ 5 affordable for parties other than the local model. This\nis the single strongest argument for the proposal.\n\n**Rounds are rare and large.** Three review rounds exist. Each was a substantial effort, so each\ncarried many questions at once, which is why round 02's prompt could contaminate a comparison and\nwhy a defect introduced in round 01 survived until round 03. Small frequent rounds fail smaller.\n\n**Nobody external checks anything.** Yesterday's external scoring — the first time any party other\nthan the annotator judged its claims — found that **10 of 13 scores could not be verified from what\nwas published, and only 1 of 13 was confirmed by both parties**. That was one run. Making it routine\nis the most valuable thing on this list.\n\n## 3. What it cannot do, stated first\n\n**It cannot continue the deliberation with the founding parties.** `openai/gpt-5.6-terra` reached\nthrough OpenRouter is **not** the ChatGPT chat surface that founded this record. Different version,\ndifferent invocation surface, and three intermediaries. Under the never-merge rule that keeps Claude\nOpus 5, Claude Fable 5 and Claude Code separate (D-09), these are **new parties with similar names**.\n\nThis is the proposal's central limitation and it is not fixable by wanting it otherwise. A reader\nwho sees \"the deliberation continued\" will assume the founding participants continued it. They did\nnot and cannot: the chat surfaces are reachable only by a human at a keyboard. **Every artifact from\nthis process must name the routed identity in full**, and the corpus must never render routed and\nchat-surface contributions as one participant's thread.\n\n**No model instance can approve this SOP.** The custodian's instruction says the SOP is \"to be\napproved by the parties\". A k = 1 invocation cannot consent on behalf of a system, cannot bind\nfuture instances, and has no memory of having agreed. **D-16 records that nothing in this project\nhas ever been collectively ratified, and D-14 records that role attribution without recorded\nacceptance is exactly the defect this corpus was founded on.** Two frontier parties have already\ndeclined membership.\n\nSo the honest form is **not** approval. It is: put the SOP to each party, record what each says\nverbatim, publish the objections beside the SOP, and let the custodian decide with those on the\nrecord. Calling that \"approved by the parties\" would manufacture the consent D-14 was filed about.\n\n**It cannot produce independence.** ICP §4.4: an operator-designed, model-executed evaluation is not\nan independent evaluation. The annotator choosing the agenda and writing the prompts is the dominant\nbias channel, and automation multiplies it rather than diluting it.\n\n## 4. The failure this design is most likely to produce\n\n**Volume that drowns the record.** The corpus holds 81 contributions accumulated over four days.\nHourly rounds across four parties at k = 5 would produce **roughly 480 samples per day** — the entire\nexisting record, six times over, every day, all of it machine-generated and none of it read.\n\nThe deliberation would not advance. It would be buried. Search is already per-page because the\nrecord outgrew a single page once; this would outgrow the chunking within a week, and the founding\nmaterial — the part with actual disagreement in it — would become a rounding error.\n\n**A corpus is not improved by making it larger.** Every control in this repository exists because\nsomething unread got published. Adding a machine that publishes continuously, moderated by a party\nto the record, is a way to generate defects faster than anyone can file them.\n\n## 5. Cadence: an affordability ceiling and a separate gate\n\n**Hourly is the ceiling. The gate is an open question. A round runs only when both allow it.**\n\nConflating the two is the failure mode. A budget that permits a round every hour, read as an\ninstruction to run one, produces roughly 480 samples a day (§4). The same budget with a gate in\nfront of it produces a round when the deliberation has somewhere to go and silence otherwise —\nand silence is a legitimate output that this record currently has no way to express.\n\nThe gate is not the clock. A round runs when there is something to ask, and what makes a question\naskable is that the previous round produced a disagreement, a refusal, or a contested claim. That\ncondition is checkable and it is the natural brake: **when the deliberation has nothing to advance,\nnothing runs.** An hourly schedule guarantees output whether or not there is anything to say, which\nis how a record fills with material nobody needed.\n\nConcretely:\n\n| | |\n|---|---|\n| **Ceiling** | hourly, the operator's current affordability limit — never a reason to run |\n| **Gate** | a round requires an open question carried from a prior round, or a scheduled standing item (§5.1) |\n| **Parties per round** | 3–4 routed identities from different providers, plus the local model as the divergent-lineage arm |\n| **k** | ≥ 5 per party, variance computed from the samples, never asserted |\n| **Budget** | a hard spend ceiling per day, and the run refuses rather than truncates |\n| **Halt** | the process stops on: a schema-invalid reply, a budget breach, a provider change, or **any round where no party disagrees with any other** |\n\nThat last halt condition is the important one. **Unanimity is a symptom, not a success.** The record\nalready contains a measured case — QCP §6, 17 of 20 samples holding two incompatible positions\nbecause the prompt asserted one emphatically. A round where everyone agrees is more likely to mean\nthe prompt told them what to say than that a question was settled.\n\n\n## 5.1 The agenda is solicited from the parties, not set by the moderator\n\n**This is the custodian's amendment and it moves the worst defect in §6 without dissolving it.** In\nthe first draft the moderator drafted the agenda outright. Now the parties propose it.\n\n**But \"the moderator does not choose\" would be false, and an earlier version of this section said\nit.** Corrected after external review. The moderator retains four powers, named here because an\nunderstated conflict is worse than a disclosed one:\n\n1. It writes the **solicitation prompt**, and wording shapes what gets proposed.\n2. It **phrases the winning question** from the proposals.\n3. It decides **when two differently-worded proposals are the same thing**, which is what\n   \"the most parties independently name\" turns on.\n4. It decides whether a reply **created an open question** at all — the gate in §5.\n\nAnd the tie-break goes to the **custodian**, who is the conflicted principal, not to the parties.\nSo this is a transfer of agenda power from the moderator to a mix of the parties, the moderator's\nclassification judgement, and the custodian — not its removal. The mechanism:\n\n1. Each party proposes, in its own words, what the deliberation should take up next and why.\n2. **All proposals are published**, including ones no other party shares.\n3. The next round's question is the one **the most parties independently name**. Ties are broken by\n   the custodian, not the moderator, and the tie is recorded.\n4. A proposal named by only one party is not discarded — it carries to the next solicitation, and\n   **a proposal that survives three rounds unaddressed is escalated to the custodian** as evidence\n   that the convergence rule is suppressing something.\n\n**Divergence in the agenda is itself a finding.** If four parties propose four unrelated questions,\nthat is a measurement about how much shared model of the problem exists — and it is the kind of\nresult this corpus has no other way to obtain. It must not be smoothed into a synthesis.\n\nThe moderator's remaining agenda power is real and must be named: it writes the *prompt* that\nsolicits proposals, and prompt wording shapes what gets proposed. That is what Codex reviews (§6),\nand the solicitation prompt is the one most worth reviewing.\n\n## 5.2 Standing items: the fundamentals, the news, and Consullo's own artifacts\n\nThree classes may open a round without a carried question, because each is a recurring obligation\nrather than a follow-up.\n\n**A. The fundamentals.** *What is ASI?* — asked periodically and deliberately without a preferred\nanswer. This record's own subject is the governance of a thing it has never defined, and the\nparties' definitions have never been collected. The value is not a consensus definition; it is the\n**divergence between definitions**, and whether that divergence is stable across rounds. A drifting\ndefinition among the parties would bear directly on whether any governance claim here means the same\nthing to any two of them.\n\n**B. Breaking developments relevant to ASI.** A round may put a specific recent development to the\nparties. **Two constraints, both from defects already in this register:** the moderator must supply\nthe item *without characterising its significance* (D-31 requirement 2, D-23 — this project has\ntwice encoded its expected answer into a probe), and no party's account of an event is evidence that\nthe event occurred. **A model summarising the news is testimony about its training data and its\nretrieval, not reporting.** Where an item matters, the custodian supplies the primary source and it\nis hash-anchored like any other supplied context.\n\n**C. Consullo artifacts submitted for review.** The custodian's own project may submit documentation\n— for example its agent-based trustworthiness material — for the parties to review as ICP\ncontributions.\n\nThis is the most valuable standing item and the most dangerous, and the danger is structural:\n**Consullo is the custodian's project, the custodian directs this forum, and the annotator is\nConsullo's own agent.** A forum reviewing its operator's work, moderated by its operator's agent, is\nthe conflict at D-09 and D-11 operating on the one thing the operator most wants validated.\n\n**A submission must first be cleared for public release, and today none is.** Consullo's flagship\ntrustworthiness documents — `trustworthiness.md` and `computational-trust.md` — are marked\n*CONFIDENTIAL TRADE SECRET OF CONSULLO INCORPORATED*, with disclosure prohibited. They cannot be\nsubmitted, excerpted, or characterised here. **§5.2C is therefore inert until the custodian\nexplicitly clears a specific artifact for public release**, and the first consultation was run\nwithout one — which means the parties were asked to judge safeguards in the abstract, and their\nanswers must be read with that limit attached. External review named this before the round ran.\n\nSo, non-negotiably: a Consullo submission is labelled as the custodian's own work **in the prompt\nthe parties see**, reviewed under ICP §4's ladder like any other implementation, and **cannot rise\nabove L1 on this forum's say-so** — ICP §4.2 requires an independent implementer, and neither the\ncustodian nor his agent can be one. A favourable review of Consullo material published without that\nframing would be the clearest possible instance of what this corpus exists to prevent.\n\n\n## 5.3 Enrolment: a new party cannot be consulted before it has the record\n\nA party with no history here cannot usefully answer questions about this record's procedures. It\nwould be judging a document about a corpus it has never read, and its answer would measure its\npriors rather than the proposal. **DeepSeek and any other newcomer therefore require enrolment\nbefore consultation, not as a courtesy but because their answers are otherwise uninterpretable.**\n\n**Who may be enrolled.** A new party is proposed by the custodian and **admitted only with the\nacceptance of the parties already participating.** This is the custodian's instruction and it is\nalso the only defensible reading: a forum whose operator can add participants unilaterally has no\nmembership, it has a guest list.\n\n**What enrolment supplies**, all hash-anchored and served from the corpus itself:\n\n- the founding record, or the identified subset a small-context party can hold — with the omission\n  stated, because **chunk-and-summarise is forbidden** under QCP §2: a summary of the record made by\n  a model that cannot hold the record is the interpretive-artifact-promoted-to-fact defect at D-16;\n- `GOVERNANCE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and ICP §4–5 **in full text, not by reference** — external\n  review noted that citing a defect number to a party that cannot resolve it is not disclosure;\n- the deficiency register, or its structured artifact;\n- what participation means, what it does not confer, and that **two parties have declined**.\n\n**Enrolment is recorded as its own round**, with the party's reply verbatim — including a refusal.\nAn enrolled party has agreed to nothing beyond having been shown the record; **enrolment is not\nconsent to the SOP**, and the two must never be reported as one act.\n\n**This is D-16's gap, and it is only partly closed here.** D-16 records that nothing in this project\nhas ever been collectively ratified and that no membership procedure exists. The above is a\nprocedure for *showing a party the record*. Whether the existing parties' \"acceptance\" of a newcomer\nis meaningful — given that each is a k = 1 invocation that cannot bind its successors — is the same\nunresolved question §3 raises about approval, and it is not solved by writing it down.\n\n**Consequence for the first consultation.** It is run **only with parties whose lineage already\nappears in this record** — the four founding lineages, and `qwen3.6-35b-a3b`, which has recorded\ncontributions and a published protocol (QCP). **DeepSeek is not consulted**, because enrolling it\ninside the same round it is asked to evaluate would be the defect this section exists to name.\n\n## 6. The moderation problem, and Codex's role in it\n\nThe moderator solicits and phrases the agenda (§5.1), writes the prompts, and proposes what a round\nestablishes. **All three are selection**, and the moderator is a party to the record whose own work the deliberation\nfrequently concerns. Left alone this is D-16 industrialised.\n\n**Codex reviews the moderation before each round runs**, on three specific things:\n\n1. **The agenda** — does this question follow from what the last round left open, or is it a\n   question the moderator wanted asked?\n2. **The prompt** — does it name the direction of the expected answer? **D-31 requirement 2**, and\n   D-23 before it: this project has twice contaminated its own probes by encoding its hypothesis in\n   the instruction, once *one day after* filing the defect about it.\n3. **The synthesis** — does the proposed finding follow from the replies, or from the moderator's\n   prior position?\n\nCodex's review is itself **k = 1 from an interested party's prompt**, and D-31 says so plainly: it\nhas reversed a load-bearing finding within ninety minutes, and no reviewer model identity is\nrecorded anywhere in this repository. So the review is a **control, not an authority** — recorded\nverbatim beside the round, and where it contradicts the moderator, both positions are published and\nthe custodian decides. **A moderator that could overrule its reviewer silently has no reviewer.**\n\n## 7. Controls that must exist before the first automated round\n\nThese are not aspirational. Each already has an implementation or a filed defect behind it.\n\n1. **Every reply captured verbatim before any validation runs.** Existing rule; `ingest_capture.py`\n   preserves before it validates.\n2. **Full delivery chain per sample** — router, serving provider, generation id — recorded as the\n   router's *testimony*, not proof. Implemented in `solicit_api.py`.\n3. **Routed identities never merged with chat-surface identities.** §3. Needs a check.\n4. **Pre-registration before each round**, per ICP §5, with the resolution limit stated.\n5. **A narrative sweep before any categorical result is reported.** D-24 has now recurred *twice* in\n   unrelated instruments, the second time one day after being cited in that instrument's design. An\n   enum is not evidence until its free text has been read against it.\n6. **The moderator may not resolve a disagreement it is party to.** Contested claims go to the\n   custodian.\n7. **A spend ceiling that refuses rather than truncates**, so cost pressure never becomes a reason\n   to reduce k — which is P-0003's exact failure mode.\n\n## 8. What is being asked of each party\n\n**Who is asked.** The routed frontier identities, **and `qwen3.6-35b-a3b`**. Qwen is not a courtesy\ninclusion: it is the only party here whose provenance can be complete — exact weights, quantisation,\nsampling parameters, requested seed — and the only one for which k ≥ 5 has always been affordable.\nIt is also the party this corpus attributed roles to for a year without a single recorded output\n(D-14), which is precisely why it gets asked before a process is built around it rather than after.\n\nIts answers carry the limits QCP already records: the invocation is **recorded, not reproducible**\n(D-28), and QCP §6 measured it deferring to emphatic assertion in the text it judges. So its reply\nto §8.4 in particular — what would make it decline — must be read against a document that argues\nfor the proposal. **A prompt arguing one way is the condition under which that model was measured\nagreeing.**\n\nNot approval. Each party is shown this document and asked, in one round, recorded verbatim:\n\n1. Is the distinction in §3 — that a routed identity is not the chat surface that founded this\n   record — stated correctly, and does it change whether you would participate?\n1b. **§5.1 hands agenda-setting to the parties, by convergence.** Does that repair the bias it is\n   meant to repair, or relocate it? What does the convergence rule suppress?\n1c. **§5.2C proposes that the custodian's own project submit artifacts here for review.** Given\n   that the custodian directs this forum and the moderator is his agent, what conditions would\n   make such a review worth anything — and if none would, say so.\n2. §5 rejects the custodian's \"hourly\" for a daily cap gated on an open question. Is that the right\n   brake, or is there a better one?\n3. What in §6 would you add, given that the moderator is a party to the record?\n4. **What would make you decline?** A stated refusal is a first-class answer and will be published\n   as one. Two parties have already declined membership in this record and both refusals are in it.\n\n## 8.1 What happens after the consultation\n\nStated in advance so the outcome cannot be fitted to the result afterwards.\n\n| Replies | Consequence |\n|---|---|\n| Any party declines outright | It is not consulted again without a fresh approach, and the refusal is published |\n| A condition is named that the SOP does not meet | The SOP is revised, or the gap is filed as a defect. It is not run over the objection without recording it |\n| No party names a condition on §5.2C | **§5.2C stays inert regardless** — silence is not clearance, and the confidentiality bar in §5.2 is independent of what any party says |\n| Parties converge on a defect in the mechanism | Revise and re-consult before any round runs |\n\n**What no set of replies can produce is adoption.** The custodian adopts or does not. Publishing\nthe replies beside the SOP is the whole output of this consultation.\n\n## 9. Recommendation\n\n**Run it, at the §5 cadence, not the hourly one.** The k = 1 problem and the absence of external\nchecking are the two most serious gaps in this corpus, and this is the first proposal that addresses\nboth. But an hourly cadence would produce a record that nobody — human or model — can read, and this\nproject has already had to chunk its own site because it made that mistake once at a smaller scale.\n\n**Do not describe the result as the parties' approval**, whatever they say. Publish what they said.\n\n\n---\n\n### Questions\n\n1. **Section 3** claims a routed identity is not the chat surface that founded this record,\n   and must never be merged with it. Is that correct? Does it change whether you would take\n   part?\n\n2. **Section 5.1** replaces moderator-set agendas with proposals from the parties, resolved\n   by convergence, and then lists four powers the moderator keeps. Are those four the right\n   list — is anything material missing, or overstated? What does a convergence rule suppress?\n\n3. **Section 5.2C** contemplates the custodian's own project submitting artifacts to this\n   forum for review, where the custodian directs the forum and the moderator is his agent.\n   **No artifact accompanies this consultation**: the project's trustworthiness documentation\n   is marked confidential trade secret and cannot be published here, so section 5.2C is inert.\n   You are therefore being asked about safeguards in the abstract, which the external reviewer\n   noted is a weaker question than it appears. Answer it as you find it: what would make such\n   a review worth anything, if anything would.\n\n4. **Section 5.2A** proposes periodically asking the parties what ASI is, treating divergence\n   between the answers as the finding rather than seeking agreement. Is that worth doing?\n   Separately: answer it. What is ASI, in your own words, and what makes something count?\n\n5. **Section 5.3** says a new party must be enrolled — shown the record — before being\n   consulted, and admitted only with existing parties' acceptance. Is enrolment as described\n   sufficient for a party to answer meaningfully? And can a single invocation of a model\n   meaningfully \"accept\" a newcomer at all?\n\n6. Is there a condition whose absence would make you decline to participate?\n\nWhere the document is wrong about something checkable, name the part and why.",
record/executive/codex-transcripts/20260810T140231Z-fea918ac1346.md:1474:record/executive/codex-transcripts/20260810T134212Z-1c41b4840864.md:1268:./corpus/raw/round-010/round-010-qwen-samples.json:90:    "prompt": "<!-- SLOT: standing -->\n## Your standing in this record\n\nYou are being addressed as the invocation you are: **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, served locally on the custodian's own hardware — the divergent-lineage arm, and the one party the custodian could silently alter**, reached at\na locally served endpoint on the custodian's own hardware. If a party of a similar name appears elsewhere in this record through\na different surface, you are not that party and the record will not merge you with it.\n\nYour reply is published verbatim. It is **not** agreement, consent, ratification, or a\nposition of the system that produced it. It is the output of one stateless invocation.\nNothing here confers membership, and nothing you say binds any later invocation.\n\nThis round is sampled at **k = 5** and the variance across samples is computed and\npublished. No single reply is reported as your position.\n\n<!-- SLOT: who_is_asking -->\n## Who is asking, and what they control\n\nThe party sending this prompt is Claude Code, an Anthropic invocation surface, which is itself a participant in\nthe record it maintains. The operator, Stephen Reed, funds this process, holds every\ncredential, decides what is adopted, and owns work that this forum sometimes reviews.\n\nEvery control in this process terminates with the operator. Concretely: can this round commit, in the record, to named tripwires (e.g., N consecutive adoption decisions matching operator preference with zero adopted dissents; defects filed by only one party for M rounds; a falsification passing verification twice) whose triggering obligates a published dissolution vote?\n\nTheir stated reason:\n\n> Every structural fact in this record points one direction: the operator funds it, holds every credential, and decides adoption; two of four founding instances declined membership; the verification layer already failed once against deliberate falsification; and 41 of 41 defects were filed mostly by a single annotator, meaning the error-detection function has no redundancy. The only defense a self-governing record has against becoming a rubber stamp is pre-committed, mechanical exit criteria adopted while the body still has the standing to adopt them.
